verses.1:1: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel across the Jordan in the wilderness plain, opposite the Red Sea, between Paran and Tophel and Laban and Hazeroth, where gold is very plentiful.
verses.1:2: It is eleven days from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir as far as Kadesh-barnea.
verses.1:3: In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses spoke to the sons of Israel all that the Lord had commanded him to say to them,
verses.1:4: after he struck down Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who stayed in Ashtaroth and in Edrei,
verses.1:5: across the Jordan in the land of Moab. And Moses began to explain the law and to say:
verses.1:6: "The Lord our God spoke to us in Horeb, saying, 'It is enough for you that you have stayed on this mountain:
verses.1:7: turn back and come to the mountain of the Amorites, and to the other regions that are nearest to it, the plains and the mountains and the lower places toward the south, and beside the shore of the sea, the land of the Canaanites and of Lebanon, as far as the great river Euphrates.
verses.1:8: Look,' He said, 'I have delivered it to you: go in and possess it, concerning which the Lord swore to your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, that He would give it to them and to their seed after them.'
verses.1:9: And I said to you at that time:
verses.1:10: 'I cannot bear you alone, because the Lord your God has multiplied you, and today you are like the stars of heaven, very numerous.
verses.1:11: (May the Lord God of your fathers add many thousands to this number, and bless you just as He has spoken.)
verses.1:12: I am not able by myself to bear your affairs, and the burden and disputes.
verses.1:13: Give from among you men who are wise and knowledgeable, and whose conduct is proven in your tribes, so that I may set them as leaders for you.'
verses.1:14: Then you answered me, 'It is a good thing that you want to do.'
verses.1:15: And I took from your tribes wise and noble men, and I appointed them as leaders: tribunes, and centurions, and officers of fifty and officers of ten, who would teach you each individual matter.
verses.1:16: And I commanded them, saying, 'Hear them, and judge what is just, whether he is a citizen or a foreigner.
verses.1:17: There shall be no distinction of persons: you shall hear the small just as the great, nor shall you favor the person of anyone, because judgment belongs to God. And if anything seems difficult to you, refer it to me, and I will hear it.'
verses.1:18: And I commanded everything that you should do.
verses.1:19: Now setting out from Horeb, we passed through a terrible and very great desert, which you saw, by the way of the mountain of the Amorite, just as the Lord our God had commanded us. And when we had come to Kadesh-barnea,
verses.1:20: I said to you, 'You have come to the mountain of the Amorite, which the Lord our God is about to give to us:
verses.1:21: see the land that the Lord your God is giving to you: go up and possess it, just as the Lord our God spoke to your fathers: do not fear, nor dread anything.'
verses.1:22: And all of you approached me and said, 'Let us send men who will examine the land and report back by which route we should go up and to which cities we should proceed.'
verses.1:23: And when the word pleased me, I sent twelve men from among you, one from each of their tribes.
verses.1:24: And when they had proceeded and gone up into the mountains, they came as far as the Valley of the Cluster; and having examined the land,
verses.1:25: taking some of its fruits so that they might show its fertility, they brought them to us and said, 'The land that the Lord our God is about to give to us is good.'
verses.1:26: And you were unwilling to go up, but being unbelieving toward the word of the Lord our God,
verses.1:27: you grumbled in your tents and said, 'The Lord hates us, and for that reason He brought us out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorite and destroy us.
verses.1:28: Where shall we go up? The messengers have terrified our heart, saying, "The multitude is very great, and taller in stature than we are; the cities are great and fortified up to heaven; we saw the sons of the Anakim there."'
verses.1:29: And I said to you, 'Do not be frightened, nor fear them:
verses.1:30: the Lord God, who is your leader, He Himself will fight for you, just as He did in Egypt while all were watching.
verses.1:31: And in the wilderness (you yourself saw it) the Lord your God carried you, as a man is accustomed to carry his little son, on all the way along which you walked, until you came to this place.'
verses.1:32: And not even so did you believe the Lord your God,
verses.1:33: who went ahead of you on the way, and marked out the place in which you should pitch tents, showing you the route by night through fire, and by day through a pillar of cloud.
verses.1:34: And when the Lord heard the voice of your words, being angry, He swore and said:
verses.1:35: 'Not one of the men of this most wicked generation will see the good land that I promised under oath to your fathers,
verses.1:36: except Caleb son of Jephunneh: for he himself will see it, and to him I will give the land that he trod upon, and to his sons, because he followed the Lord.'
verses.1:37: Nor is the indignation against the people surprising, since the Lord, being angry with me also on account of you, said, 'Neither will you go in there;
verses.1:38: but Joshua son of Nun, your attendant, he himself will enter in your place. Encourage and strengthen him, and he himself will divide the land by lot for Israel.
verses.1:39: Your little ones, about whom you said that they would be led away captive, and the children who today do not know the distinction between good and evil, they themselves will go in; and to them I will give the land, and they will possess it.
verses.1:40: But as for you, turn back and depart into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.'
verses.1:41: And you answered me, 'We have sinned against the Lord: we will go up and fight, just as the Lord our God has commanded.' And when, equipped with weapons, you were proceeding into the mountain,
verses.1:42: the Lord said to me, 'Say to them, "Do not go up, nor fight, for I am not with you, so that you do not fall before your enemies."'
verses.1:43: I spoke, and you did not listen; but opposing the command of the Lord, and swelling with pride, you went up into the mountain.
verses.1:44: Therefore the Amorite who lived in the mountains came out, and coming to meet you, pursued you, just as bees are accustomed to pursue, and struck you down from Seir as far as Hormah.
verses.1:45: And when you returned and wept before the Lord, He did not listen to you, nor was He willing to yield to your voice.
verses.1:46: Therefore you remained in Kadesh-barnea for a long time."
verses.2:1: And setting out from there, we came into the wilderness that leads to the Red Sea, just as the Lord had said to me; and we went around Mount Seir for a long time.
verses.2:2: And the Lord said to me:
verses.2:3: "It is enough for you to go around this mountain; go toward the north,
verses.2:4: and command the people, saying, 'You will pass through the territory of your brothers, the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, and they will fear you.
verses.2:5: Watch carefully, therefore, that you do not move against them. For I will not give you as much of their land as the sole of one foot can tread on, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.
verses.2:6: You will buy food from them with money and eat; you will draw water that you have bought and drink.'"
verses.2:7: The Lord your God has blessed you in every work of your hands; He knows your journey, how you passed through this great wilderness, the Lord your God living with you for forty years, and nothing was lacking to you.
verses.2:8: And when we had passed by our brothers, the sons of Esau, who lived in Seir, by the way of the plain from Elath and from Ezion-geber, we came to the road that leads into the desert of Moab.
verses.2:9: And the Lord said to me, "Do not fight against the Moabites, nor enter into battle against them; for I will not give you anything from their land, because I have handed Ar over to the sons of Lot as a possession."
verses.2:10: The Emim were its first inhabitants, a great and strong people, and so tall that, as of the lineage of the Anakim,
verses.2:11: they were thought to be like giants and were like the sons of the Anakim. Indeed, the Moabites call them Emim.
verses.2:12: Now the Horites previously lived in Seir; after they were driven out and destroyed, the sons of Esau lived there, just as Israel did in the land of its possession, which the Lord gave to it.
verses.2:13: Rising, therefore, to cross the stream of Zered, we came to it.
verses.2:14: Now the time during which we walked from Kadesh-barnea until the crossing of the stream of Zered was thirty-eight years, until the entire generation of the men of war was consumed from the camp, just as the Lord had sworn,
verses.2:15: whose hand was against them, so that they would perish from the middle of the camp.
verses.2:16: Now after all the warriors had fallen,
verses.2:17: the Lord spoke to me, saying:
verses.2:18: "Today you will cross the borders of Moab, the city named Ar;
verses.2:19: and approaching the vicinity of the sons of Ammon, be careful not to fight against them, nor move to battle; for I will not give you any of the land of the sons of Ammon, because I have given it to the sons of Lot as a possession."
verses.2:20: It was considered a land of giants; and giants formerly lived in it, whom the Ammonites call Zamzummim,
verses.2:21: a great and numerous people, and of tall stature, like the Anakim, whom the Lord destroyed from before their face; and He made them live in their place,
verses.2:22: just as He had done for the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, destroying the Horites and handing their land over to them, which they possess to the present.
verses.2:23: The Cappadocians also drove out the Hivites, who lived in Hazerim as far as Gaza; coming out of Cappadocia, they destroyed them and lived in their place.
verses.2:24: "Rise and cross the stream of Arnon; look, I have handed over into your hand Sihon king of Heshbon, the Amorite, and begin to possess his land, and engage in battle against him.
verses.2:25: Today I will begin to send the terror and dread of you upon the peoples who live under the whole heaven, so that when your name is heard, they will be terrified, and tremble like women in labor, and be gripped by pain."
verses.2:26: Therefore I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with peaceful words, saying:
verses.2:27: "We will pass through your land; we will walk along the public road; we will not turn aside either to the right or to the left.
verses.2:28: Sell us provisions for a price so that we may eat; supply water for money, and so we will drink. Only this, that you grant us passage,
verses.2:29: just as the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, and the Moabites, who reside in Ar, did, until we come to the Jordan and cross over to the land that the Lord our God is about to give us."
verses.2:30: And Sihon king of Heshbon was unwilling to give us passage, because the Lord your God had hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, so that he would be handed over into your hands, just as you see now.
verses.2:31: And the Lord said to me, "Look, I have begun to hand Sihon and his land over to you; begin to possess it."
verses.2:32: And Sihon came out to meet us with all his people for battle at Jahaz.
verses.2:33: And the Lord our God handed him over to us; and we struck him down with his sons and all his people.
verses.2:34: And we captured all the cities at that time, having killed their inhabitants, men and women and little ones; we left nothing in them,
verses.2:35: apart from the livestock, which came as the share of the plunderers, and the spoils of the cities that we captured
verses.2:36: from Aroer, which is on the bank of the stream of Arnon, the town that is situated in the valley, as far as Gilead. There was not a village or city that escaped our hands; the Lord our God handed all of them over to us,
verses.2:37: apart from the land of the sons of Ammon, which we did not approach, and all that adjoins the stream of Jabbok, and the mountain cities, and all the places from which the Lord our God barred us.
verses.3:1: And so, turning, we went up by the road of Bashan; and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us with his people to wage war at Edrei.
verses.3:2: And the Lord said to me, "Do not fear him, because he has been handed over into your hand with all his people and his land; and you will do to him just as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
verses.3:3: Therefore the Lord our God handed over into our hands Og king of Bashan also, and all his people; and we struck them down to utter destruction,
verses.3:4: devastating all his cities at one time. There was not a town that escaped us: sixty cities, the entire region of Argob of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
verses.3:5: All the cities were fortified with very high walls, gates, and bars, apart from countless towns that had no walls.
verses.3:6: And we destroyed them, just as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, wiping out every city, men and women and little ones;
verses.3:7: but we plundered the livestock and the spoils of the cities.
verses.3:8: And at that time we took the land from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were across the Jordan, from the stream of Arnon as far as Mount Hermon,
verses.3:9: which the Sidonians call Sirion, and the Amorites Senir:
verses.3:10: all the cities that are situated on the plain, and the entire land of Gilead and Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
verses.3:11: For Og king of Bashan alone had remained from the lineage of the giants. His iron bed is shown, which is in Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, having nine cubits in length and four in width according to the measure of the cubit of a man's hand.
verses.3:12: And we took possession of the land at that time from Aroer, which is on the bank of the stream of Arnon, as far as half of Mount Gilead; and I gave its cities to Reuben and Gad.
verses.3:13: Now the remaining part of Gilead, and all Bashan of the kingdom of Og, I handed over to the half-tribe of Manasseh, the entire region of Argob; and all Bashan is called the Land of Giants.
verses.3:14: Jair the son of Manasseh took possession of the entire region of Argob as far as the borders of the Geshurites and the Maacathites. And he called Bashan after his own name Havvoth-jair, that is, the Villages of Jair, to the present day.
verses.3:15: To Machir also I gave Gilead.
verses.3:16: And to the tribes of Reuben and Gad I gave from the land of Gilead as far as the stream of Arnon, the middle of the stream, and the boundary as far as the stream of Jabbok, which is the border of the sons of Ammon,
verses.3:17: and the plain of the wilderness, and the Jordan, and the borders of Chinnereth as far as the sea of the desert, which is the saltiest, at the foot of Mount Pisgah toward the east.
verses.3:18: And I commanded you at that time, saying, "The Lord your God is giving you this land as an inheritance; go armed ahead of your brothers, the sons of Israel, all you strong men,
verses.3:19: apart from your wives, little ones, and livestock. For I know that you have many herds, and they must remain in the cities that I handed over to you,
verses.3:20: until the Lord grants rest to your brothers, just as He granted to you, and they themselves also possess the land that He is about to give them across the Jordan; then each one will return to his own possession, which I gave to you."
verses.3:21: I also commanded Joshua at that time, saying, "Your eyes have seen what the Lord your God did to these two kings; so He will do to all the kingdoms to which you are about to cross over.
verses.3:22: Do not fear them, for the Lord your God will fight for you."
verses.3:23: And I prayed to the Lord at that time, saying:
verses.3:24: "Lord God, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your very strong hand; for there is no other god either in heaven or on earth who can do Your works and be compared to Your strength.
verses.3:25: Therefore I will cross over and see this finest land across the Jordan, and this splendid mountain, and Lebanon."
verses.3:26: And the Lord was angry with me because of you, and did not listen to me, but said to me, "It is enough for you; never speak to Me again about this matter.
verses.3:27: Go up to the summit of Pisgah, and turn your eyes around to the west, and to the north, and south, and east, and look; for you will not cross this Jordan.
verses.3:28: Command Joshua, and strengthen him and encourage him, because he himself will go ahead of this people, and he will divide for them the land that you are about to see."
verses.3:29: And we stayed in the valley opposite the shrine of Peor.
verses.4:1: And now, Israel, listen to the precepts and judgments that I teach you, so that, doing them, you may live, and entering in, you may possess the land that the Lord God of your fathers is about to give to you.
verses.4:2: You must not add to the word that I am speaking to you, nor subtract from it; keep the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you.
verses.4:3: Your eyes have seen all that the Lord did against Baal-peor, how He crushed all his worshipers from your midst.
verses.4:4: But you who hold fast to the Lord your God are all alive to the present day.
verses.4:5: You know that I have taught you precepts and just decrees, just as the Lord my God commanded me; so you will do them in the land that you are about to possess,
verses.4:6: and you will observe and fulfill them in deed. For this is your wisdom and understanding before the peoples, so that, hearing all these precepts, they may say, "Look, a wise and understanding people, a great nation."
verses.4:7: Nor is there another nation so great that has gods drawing near to it, as our God is present at all our pleas.
verses.4:8: For what other nation is so renowned that it has ceremonies, just judgments, and the entire law that I will set before your eyes today?
verses.4:9: Guard yourself, therefore, and your soul carefully. Do not forget the words that your eyes have seen, and do not let them slip from your heart all the days of your life. You will teach them to your sons and grandsons,
verses.4:10: from the day on which you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb, when the Lord spoke to me, saying, "Gather the people to Me, so that they may hear My words, and learn to fear Me all the time that they live on the earth, and teach their sons."
verses.4:11: And you came near to the foot of the mountain, which was burning up to heaven; and on it were darkness, cloud, and dense gloom.
verses.4:12: And the Lord spoke to you from the midst of the fire. You heard the sound of His words, and you saw no form at all.
verses.4:13: And He showed you His covenant, which He commanded you to do, and the ten words, which He wrote on two stone tablets.
verses.4:14: And at that time He commanded me to teach you the ceremonies and judgments that you ought to do in the land that you are about to possess.
verses.4:15: Guard your souls carefully, therefore. You did not see any likeness on the day when the Lord spoke to you at Horeb from the midst of the fire,
verses.4:16: so that you might not be deceived and make for yourselves a carved likeness, or an image of male or female,
verses.4:17: a likeness of all beasts that are on the earth, or of birds flying under heaven,
verses.4:18: and of crawling creatures that move on the earth, or of fish that dwell beneath the earth in the waters;
verses.4:19: so that, lifting your eyes to heaven, you might not see the sun and the moon and all the stars of heaven, and, deceived by error, worship them and serve what the Lord your God created for the service of all the nations that are under heaven.
verses.4:20: You, however, the Lord took and led out of the iron furnace of Egypt, so that He might have a people of inheritance, as it is on the present day.
verses.4:21: And the Lord became angry against me because of your words, and swore that I would not cross the Jordan, nor enter the finest land that He is about to give to you.
verses.4:22: Look, I am dying on this soil; I will not cross the Jordan; you will cross and possess the excellent land.
verses.4:23: Be careful that you never forget the covenant of the Lord your God, which He made with you, nor make for yourself a carved likeness of those things that the Lord has forbidden to be made;
verses.4:24: because the Lord your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.
verses.4:25: If you have fathered sons and grandsons, and have remained in the land, and, being deceived, have made for yourselves any likeness, committing evil before the Lord your God so as to provoke Him to anger,
verses.4:26: I call upon heaven and earth today as witnesses that you will swiftly perish from the land which, after crossing the Jordan, you are about to possess; you will not live in it for a long time, but the Lord will destroy you,
verses.4:27: and scatter you among all the peoples, and you will remain few among the nations to which the Lord is about to lead you.
verses.4:28: And there you will serve gods that have been crafted by the hand of men, wood and stone that do not see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
verses.4:29: And when you seek the Lord your God there, you will find Him, provided that you seek Him with your whole heart and with all the affliction of your soul.
verses.4:30: After all the things that were foretold have found you, in the last time you will return to the Lord your God and listen to His voice.
verses.4:31: For the Lord your God is a merciful God; He will not abandon you, nor utterly destroy you, nor will He forget the covenant in which He swore to your fathers.
verses.4:32: Inquire about the ancient days that were before you, from the day on which God created man upon the earth, from one end of heaven to the other, whether a thing of this kind has ever happened, or has ever been known,
verses.4:33: that a people should hear the voice of God speaking from the midst of the fire, just as you heard and lived;
verses.4:34: whether God has acted so as to go in and take a nation for Himself from the midst of the nations, through trials, signs, and wonders, through battle and a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and terrifying visions, according to all that the Lord your God did for you in Egypt while your eyes looked on;
verses.4:35: so that you might know that the Lord Himself is God, and there is no other besides Him.
verses.4:36: From heaven He caused you to hear His voice, so that He might teach you, and on earth He showed you His very great fire, and you heard His words from the midst of the fire,
verses.4:37: because He loved your fathers and chose their seed after them. And going ahead in His great power, He led you out of Egypt,
verses.4:38: so that He might destroy nations very great and stronger than you at your entry, and bring you in, and give you their land as a possession, as you see on the present day.
verses.4:39: Know, therefore, today, and reflect in your heart that the Lord Himself is God in heaven above and on earth below, and there is no other.
verses.4:40: Keep His precepts and commandments, which I command you, so that it may go well for you and for your sons after you, and that you may remain for a long time upon the land that the Lord your God is about to give to you.
verses.4:41: Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan toward the eastern region,
verses.4:42: so that one who has unintentionally killed his neighbor, and was not his enemy a day or two before, might flee to them and be able to escape to one of these cities:
verses.4:43: Bezer in the wilderness, which is situated in the level land of the tribe of Reuben; and Ramoth in Gilead, which is in the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, which is in the tribe of Manasseh.
verses.4:44: This is the law that Moses set before the sons of Israel,
verses.4:45: and these are the testimonies and ceremonies and judgments that he spoke to the sons of Israel when they came out of Egypt,
verses.4:46: beyond the Jordan in the valley opposite the shrine of Peor, in the land of Sihon, the Amorite king, who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses struck down. The sons of Israel also, having come out of Egypt,
verses.4:47: took possession of his land and the land of Og, king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun,
verses.4:48: from Aroer, which is situated on the bank of the stream of Arnon, as far as Mount Sion, which is also Hermon,
verses.4:49: all the plain beyond the Jordan toward the eastern region, as far as the sea of the wilderness, and as far as the foot of Mount Pisgah.
verses.5:1: And Moses called all Israel and said to them, "Hear, Israel, the ceremonies and judgments that I speak in your ears today; learn them and fulfill them in deed.
verses.5:2: The Lord our God established a covenant with us at Horeb.
verses.5:3: Not with our fathers did He enter into the covenant, but with us who are here at the present time and live.
verses.5:4: Face to face He spoke to us on the mountain from the midst of the fire.
verses.5:5: I was the mediator and intermediary between the Lord and you at that time, to declare His words to you, for you feared the fire and did not go up onto the mountain. And He said:
verses.5:6: 'I am the Lord your God, who led you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.
verses.5:7: You shall not have foreign gods in My sight.
verses.5:8: You shall not make for yourself a sculpted image, nor a likeness of any of the things that are in heaven above, and that are on the earth below, and that move about in the waters beneath the earth.
verses.5:9: You shall not worship them, and you shall not revere them. For I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, repaying the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation, to those who hate Me,
verses.5:10: and showing mercy to many thousands, to those who love Me and keep My precepts.
verses.5:11: You shall not use the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the one who takes up His name over an empty matter will not go unpunished.
verses.5:12: Observe the Sabbath day so that you may sanctify it, just as the Lord your God commanded you.
verses.5:13: For six days you shall work and do all your works.
verses.5:14: The seventh day is the Sabbath, that is, the rest of the Lord your God. On it you shall not do any work: neither you, nor your son, nor daughter, nor male servant, nor female servant, nor ox, nor donkey, nor any beast of burden of yours, nor the foreigner who is within your gates, so that your male servant and your female servant may rest, just as you also do.
verses.5:15: Remember that you yourself also were a slave in Egypt, and the Lord your God led you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore He commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.
verses.5:16: Honor your father and mother, just as the Lord your God commanded you, so that you may live for a long time and it may go well with you in the land that the Lord your God is about to give to you.
verses.5:17: And you shall not commit adultery.
verses.5:19: and you shall not commit theft;
verses.5:20: nor shall you speak false testimony against your neighbor.
verses.5:21: You shall not covet the wife of your neighbor: neither house, nor field, nor male servant, nor female servant, nor ox, nor donkey, nor anything at all that belongs to him.'
verses.5:22: These words the Lord spoke to your whole multitude on the mountain from the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the thick gloom, with a loud voice, adding nothing further; and He wrote them on two stone tablets, which He delivered to me.
verses.5:23: Then after you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness and saw the mountain burning, you approached me, all the leaders of the tribes and the elders, and said:
verses.5:24: 'Look, the Lord our God has shown us His majesty and greatness; we have heard His voice from the midst of the fire, and we have proved today that when God speaks with man, man has lived.
verses.5:25: Why then will we die, and will this enormous fire devour us? For if we hear the voice of the Lord our God any further, we will die.
verses.5:26: What is all flesh, that it should hear the voice of the living God, who speaks from the midst of the fire just as we have heard, and be able to live?
verses.5:27: Rather, you draw near and hear all the things that the Lord our God will say to you; and you will speak to us, and listening, we will do them.'
verses.5:28: When the Lord had heard this, He said to me, 'I have heard the voice of the words of this people that they have spoken to you; they have spoken all things well.
verses.5:29: Who would grant that they might have such a mind, to fear Me and keep all My commandments at all times, so that it might go well with them and their children forever?
verses.5:30: Go and say to them, "Return to your tents."
verses.5:31: But you, stand here with Me, and I will speak to you all My commandments, and ceremonies, and judgments, which you will teach them, so that they may do them in the land that I will give to them as a possession.'
verses.5:32: Therefore keep and do the things that the Lord God has commanded you; you shall not turn aside either to the right or to the left,
verses.5:33: but you shall walk along the way that the Lord your God has commanded, so that you may live, and it may go well with you, and days may be lengthened in the land of your possession."
verses.6:1: These are the precepts, and ceremonies, and judgments that the Lord your God commanded that I teach you, and that you do them in the land that you are crossing over to possess,
verses.6:2: so that you may fear the Lord your God and keep all His commandments and precepts, which I command you and your children and your grandchildren, all the days of your life, so that your days may be prolonged.
verses.6:3: Hear, Israel, and take care that you do what the Lord has commanded you, so that it may go well with you and you may be multiplied even more, just as the Lord, the God of your fathers, promised you a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.6:4: Hear, Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord.
verses.6:5: You shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart, and from your whole soul, and from your whole strength.
verses.6:6: And these words, which I command you today, shall be in your heart;
verses.6:7: and you shall recount them to your children, and meditate on them sitting in your house and walking on the road, sleeping and rising up.
verses.6:8: And you shall bind them like a sign on your hand, and they shall be and move between your eyes,
verses.6:9: and you shall write them on the threshold and the doors of your house.
verses.6:10: And when the Lord your God has brought you into the land regarding which He swore to your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and has given you great and most excellent cities that you did not build,
verses.6:11: houses full of all riches, which you did not construct, cisterns that you did not dig, vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant, and you have eaten and been satisfied, be very careful not to forget the Lord, who led you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery. You shall fear the Lord your God, and Him alone you shall serve, and by His name you shall swear.
verses.6:14: You shall not go after the foreign gods of all the nations that are around you,
verses.6:15: because the Lord your God in your midst is a jealous God; otherwise the fury of the Lord your God might at some time be provoked against you and remove you from the surface of the earth.
verses.6:16: You shall not test the Lord your God, just as you tested Him at the place of testing.
verses.6:17: Keep the precepts of the Lord your God, and the testimonies and ceremonies that He commanded you,
verses.6:18: and do what is pleasing and good in the sight of the Lord, so that it may go well with you, and entering in you may possess the most excellent land about which the Lord swore to your fathers,
verses.6:19: that He would wipe out all your enemies before you, just as He has spoken.
verses.6:20: And when your son asks you tomorrow, saying, "What do these testimonies, and ceremonies, and judgments mean, which the Lord our God commanded us?"
verses.6:21: you shall say to him, "We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, and the Lord led us out from Egypt with a strong hand,
verses.6:22: and He performed signs and wonders, great and most grievous, in Egypt against Pharaoh and his whole house in our sight,
verses.6:23: and He led us out from there, so that, having brought us in, He might give us the land concerning which He swore to our fathers.
verses.6:24: And the Lord commanded us to do all these ordinances and to fear the Lord our God, so that it may go well with us all the days of our life, just as it is today.
verses.6:25: And He will be merciful to us, if we keep and do all His precepts before the Lord our God, just as He commanded us."
verses.7:1: When the Lord your God brings you into the land that you will enter to possess, and wipes out many nations before you, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations far greater in number than you are and stronger than you,
verses.7:2: and the Lord your God hands them over to you, you shall strike them down to utter destruction. You shall not enter into a covenant with them, nor show mercy to them,
verses.7:3: nor shall you form marriages with them. You shall not give your daughter to his son, nor shall you take his daughter for your son,
verses.7:4: for she will lead your son astray, so that he does not follow Me and instead serves foreign gods; and the fury of the Lord will be enraged, and He will wipe you out quickly.
verses.7:5: Rather, you shall do these things to them: overturn their altars, and shatter the statues, and cut down the groves, and burn up the carved images.
verses.7:6: For you are a holy people to the Lord your God. The Lord your God has chosen you so that you may be a special people to Him out of all the peoples who are on the earth.
verses.7:7: Not because you surpassed all the nations in number did the Lord join Himself to you and choose you, since you are fewer than all the peoples,
verses.7:8: but because the Lord loved you and kept the oath that He swore to your fathers; and He brought you out with a strong hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
verses.7:9: And you will know that the Lord your God, He Himself is the mighty and faithful God, keeping covenant and mercy for those who love Him and for those who keep His precepts, to a thousand generations,
verses.7:10: and repaying those who hate Him immediately, so as to destroy them and delay no longer, at once paying them back what they deserve.
verses.7:11: Keep, therefore, the precepts and ceremonies and judgments that I command you today to do.
verses.7:12: If, after you have heard these judgments, you keep them and do them, the Lord your God will also keep for you the covenant and the mercy that He swore to your fathers,
verses.7:13: and He will love you and multiply you, and He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land, your grain, vintage, oil, herds, and the flocks of your sheep, on the land about which He swore to your fathers that He would give it to you.
verses.7:14: You will be blessed among all peoples. There will not be among you any barren one of either sex, both among people and among your flocks.
verses.7:15: The Lord will take away every sickness from you; and the worst diseases of Egypt, which you know, He will not bring upon you, but upon all your enemies.
verses.7:16: You will devour all the peoples whom the Lord your God is about to give to you. Your eye shall not spare them, nor shall you serve their gods, so that they may not become your ruin.
verses.7:17: If you say in your heart, "These nations are more numerous than I; how will I be able to wipe them out?"
verses.7:18: do not be afraid, but remember what the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and to all the Egyptians,
verses.7:19: the very great plagues that your eyes saw, and the signs and wonders, and the strong hand and outstretched arm, so that the Lord your God might bring you out; so He will do to all the peoples whom you dread.
verses.7:20: Moreover, the Lord your God will also send hornets among them, until He wipes out and destroys all who have fled from you and have been able to hide.
verses.7:21: You shall not fear them, for the Lord your God is in your midst, a great and terrifying God.
verses.7:22: He Himself will consume these nations in your sight little by little and in parts. You will not be able to wipe them out all at once, so that the beasts of the land might not multiply against you.
verses.7:23: And the Lord your God will give them over in your sight, and He will put them to death until they are completely wiped out.
verses.7:24: And He will hand their kings over into your hands, and you will destroy their names under heaven; no one will be able to resist you until you crush them.
verses.7:25: You shall burn up their carved images with fire; you shall not covet the silver and gold from which they are made, nor shall you take anything from them for yourself, so that you do not stumble, because it is an abomination to your Lord;
verses.7:26: nor shall you bring anything from an idol into your house, so that you do not become anathema, just as it also is. You shall detest it like filth, and you shall hold it in abomination like defilement and grime, because it is anathema.
verses.8:1: Be diligently careful to do every commandment that I command you today, so that you may be able to live and be multiplied, and, having entered, possess the land about which the Lord swore to your fathers.
verses.8:2: And you shall remember the entire journey along which the Lord your God led you for forty years through the desert, so that He might afflict you and test you, and that what was turning over in your mind might become known, whether you would keep His commandments or not.
verses.8:3: He afflicted you with scarcity and gave you manna as food, which you and your fathers did not know, so that He might show you that a human being does not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes out from the mouth of God.
verses.8:4: Your garment, with which you were covered, did not wear out at all with age, and your foot was not worn sore; look, it is the fortieth year,
verses.8:5: so that you may reflect in your heart that just as a man trains his son, so the Lord your God has trained you,
verses.8:6: so that you may keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and walk in His ways, and fear Him.
verses.8:7: For the Lord your God will bring you into a good land, a land of streams, waters, and springs, in whose plains and mountains the depths of rivers burst forth,
verses.8:8: a land of wheat, barley, and vineyards, in which figs, pomegranates, and olive groves grow; a land of oil and honey,
verses.8:9: where without any scarcity you will eat your bread and thoroughly enjoy an abundance of all things; its stones are iron, and from its mountains copper ores are dug,
verses.8:10: so that when you have eaten and are satisfied, you may bless the Lord your God for the excellent land that He has given you.
verses.8:11: Watch closely and be on guard so that you never forget the Lord your God and neglect His commandments, judgments, and ceremonies, which I command you today;
verses.8:12: otherwise, after you have eaten and are satisfied, and have built beautiful houses and lived in them,
verses.8:13: and have herds of cattle and flocks of sheep, and plenty of silver and gold and of all things,
verses.8:14: your heart might be lifted up, and you might fail to remember the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery,
verses.8:15: and was your guide in the great and terrifying wilderness, in which there was the serpent scorching with its breath, and the scorpion, and the dipsas, and no waters at all; who brought streams out of the hardest rock,
verses.8:16: and fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know. And after He afflicted and proved you, in the end He had mercy on you,
verses.8:17: so that you would not say in your heart, "My might and the strength of my hand have provided all these things for me,"
verses.8:18: but would remember the Lord your God, that He Himself has given you strength, so that He might fulfill His covenant concerning which He swore to your fathers, just as the present day shows.
verses.8:19: But if, forgetting the Lord your God, you follow foreign gods and worship them and adore them, look, now I foretell to you that you will completely perish.
verses.8:20: Just as the nations that the Lord wiped out at your entrance, so you also will perish, if you are disobedient to the voice of the Lord your God.
verses.9:1: Hear, Israel: you will cross the Jordan today to possess very great nations, stronger than you, huge cities, walled all the way to heaven,
verses.9:2: a great and tall people, the sons of the Anakim, whom you yourself have seen and heard, whom no one can resist face to face.
verses.9:3: Therefore you will know today that the Lord your God Himself will cross over before you, a devouring and consuming fire, who will crush them, and wipe them out and destroy them quickly before your face, just as He spoke to you.
verses.9:4: Do not say in your heart, when the Lord your God has wiped them out in your sight, "Because of my righteousness the Lord has brought me in to possess this land," whereas because of their own wicked deeds those nations have been wiped out.
verses.9:5: For it is not because of your righteous deeds and the uprightness of your heart that you will enter to possess their lands, but because they acted wickedly, at your entering they have been wiped out; and so that the Lord might fulfill His word, which He promised under oath to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.9:6: Know, therefore, that it is not because of your righteous deeds that the Lord your God has given you this excellent land as a possession, since you are a very stiff-necked people.
verses.9:7: Remember, and do not forget, how you provoked the Lord your God to anger in the wilderness. From the day on which you came out of Egypt up to this place, you have always contended against the Lord.
verses.9:8: For even at Horeb you provoked Him, and being angry, He wanted to wipe you out,
verses.9:9: when I went up onto the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that the Lord made with you; and I remained on the mountain for forty days and nights, not eating bread and not drinking water.
verses.9:10: And the Lord gave me two stone tablets written by the finger of God, and containing all the words that He spoke to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire, when the assembly of the people was gathered together.
verses.9:11: And when forty days and as many nights had passed, the Lord gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant,
verses.9:12: and said to me, "Rise, and go down from here quickly, because your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have quickly abandoned the way that you showed them, and they have made a molten image for themselves."
verses.9:13: And again the Lord said to me, "I see that this people is stiff-necked;
verses.9:14: leave Me alone, so that I may crush them and wipe out their name from under heaven, and appoint you over a nation that is greater and stronger than this one."
verses.9:15: And as I was coming down from the burning mountain and was holding the two tablets of the covenant in both hands,
verses.9:16: and saw that you had sinned against the Lord your God, and had made a molten calf for yourselves, and had quickly abandoned His way, which He had shown you,
verses.9:17: I threw the tablets from my hands and shattered them in your sight.
verses.9:18: And I fell down before the Lord as at first, for forty days and nights not eating bread and not drinking water, because of all your sins that you committed against the Lord; and you provoked Him to anger.
verses.9:19: For I feared His indignation and wrath, with which, stirred up against you, He wanted to wipe you out. And the Lord listened to me this time as well.
verses.9:20: Fiercely angry against Aaron as well, He wanted to crush him, and I pleaded for him in the same way.
verses.9:21: And seizing your sin that you had made, that is, the calf, I burned it with fire, and crushing it into pieces and reducing it completely to dust, I threw it into the stream that comes down from the mountain.
verses.9:22: At the Burning also, and at the Testing, and at the Graves of Craving, you provoked the Lord;
verses.9:23: and when He sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, "Go up, and possess the land that I have given you," you despised the command of the Lord your God, and did not believe Him, nor were you willing to listen to His voice;
verses.9:24: but you have always been rebellious from the day that I began to know you.
verses.9:25: And I lay before the Lord for forty days and nights, during which I humbly pleaded with Him that He would not wipe you out, as He had threatened;
verses.9:26: and praying, I said, "Lord God, do not destroy Your people and Your inheritance, whom You redeemed in Your greatness, whom You brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.
verses.9:27: Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; do not look upon the hardness of this people, nor its wickedness and sin,
verses.9:28: so that the inhabitants of the land from which You brought us out may not perhaps say, 'The Lord was not able to bring them into the land that He promised them, and He hated them; therefore He brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.'
verses.9:29: They are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out in Your great strength and with Your outstretched arm."
verses.10:1: At that time the Lord said to me, "Carve for yourself two stone tablets, just as the former ones were, and come up to Me onto the mountain, and you will make a wooden ark,
verses.10:2: and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the ones that you shattered earlier, and you will put them in the ark."
verses.10:3: Therefore I made an ark of acacia wood. And when I had carved two stone tablets like the former ones, I went up onto the mountain, having them in my hands.
verses.10:4: And He wrote on the tablets, according to what He had written previously, the ten words that the Lord spoke to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire, when the people were gathered together; and He gave them to me.
verses.10:5: And turning back from the mountain, I came down, and put the tablets into the ark that I had made, and they are there until now, just as the Lord commanded me.
verses.10:6: Now the sons of Israel moved camp from Beeroth of the sons of Jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and in his place his son Eleazar served in the priesthood.
verses.10:7: From there they came to Gudgodah; and setting out from that place, they camped at Jotbathah, in a land of waters and streams.
verses.10:8: At that time He set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and to stand before Him in ministry, and to bless in His name until the present day.
verses.10:9: For this reason Levi did not have a portion or a possession with his brothers, because the Lord Himself is his possession, just as the Lord your God promised him.
verses.10:10: Now I stood on the mountain, as at first, for forty days and nights; and the Lord listened to me this time as well, and was unwilling to destroy you.
verses.10:11: And He said to me, "Go, and go ahead of the people, so that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their fathers to hand over to them."
verses.10:12: And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you, except that you fear the Lord your God, and walk in His ways, and love Him, and serve the Lord your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul,
verses.10:13: and keep the commandments of the Lord and His ceremonies, which I command you today, so that it may be well with you?
verses.10:14: Look, to the Lord your God belong heaven, and the heaven of heaven, the earth, and all things that are in it;
verses.10:15: and yet the Lord was closely joined to your fathers, and loved them, and chose their seed after them, that is, you, from all the nations, just as is confirmed today.
verses.10:16: Circumcise, therefore, the foreskin of your heart, and do not harden your neck any longer;
verses.10:17: for the Lord your God Himself is God of gods and Lord of those who rule, the great, mighty, and fearsome God, who shows no partiality, nor accepts gifts.
verses.10:18: He executes justice for the orphan and the widow; He loves the foreigner, and gives him food and clothing.
verses.10:19: Therefore love foreigners yourselves, because you also were strangers in the land of Egypt.
verses.10:20: You will fear the Lord your God, and serve Him alone; you will cling to Him, and swear in His name.
verses.10:21: He Himself is your praise and your God, who has done for you these great and fearsome deeds, which your eyes have seen.
verses.10:22: With seventy souls your fathers went down into Egypt, and look, now the Lord your God has multiplied you like the stars of heaven.
verses.11:1: Love the Lord your God, therefore, and observe His precepts and ceremonies, judgments and commandments, at all times.
verses.11:2: Know today what your children do not know, who have not seen the discipline of the Lord your God, His mighty deeds and strong hand and outstretched arm,
verses.11:3: the signs and works that He did in the midst of Egypt to Pharaoh the king and to all his land,
verses.11:4: and to the entire army of the Egyptians, and to the horses and chariots: how the waters of the Red Sea covered them while they were pursuing you, and the Lord destroyed them up to the present day;
verses.11:5: and what He did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place,
verses.11:6: and to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, who was the son of Reuben, whom the earth swallowed up when it opened its mouth, together with their households and tents and all their possessions that they had in the midst of Israel.
verses.11:7: Your eyes have seen the great works of the Lord that He did,
verses.11:8: so that you may keep all His commandments that I command you today, and may be able to enter and possess the land into which you are going,
verses.11:9: and may live for a long time in it, the land that the Lord promised under oath to your fathers and to their seed, flowing with milk and honey.
verses.11:10: For the land that you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came out, where, once the seed has been sown, irrigating waters are channeled in the manner of gardens;
verses.11:11: but it is mountainous and has plains, awaiting rains from heaven,
verses.11:12: which the Lord your God always looks after, and His eyes are upon it from the beginning of the year to its end.
verses.11:13: If therefore you obey my commandments that I command you today, to love the Lord your God and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,
verses.11:14: He will give rain to your land, early and late, so that you may gather grain, wine, and oil,
verses.11:15: and hay from the fields to feed the livestock, and so that you yourselves may eat and be satisfied.
verses.11:16: Be careful, or your heart may somehow be deceived, and you may turn away from the Lord, and serve foreign gods and worship them,
verses.11:17: and the Lord, growing angry, may shut heaven, and the rains may not come down, nor may the earth yield its produce, and you may perish quickly from the excellent land that the Lord is about to give you.
verses.11:18: Place these words of mine in your hearts and in your souls, and hang them as a sign on your hands, and set them between your eyes.
verses.11:19: Teach your children to meditate on them, when you sit in your house, and walk along the way, and lie down and rise up.
verses.11:20: You shall write them on the doorposts and doors of your house,
verses.11:21: so that your days and those of your children may be multiplied in the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give them, as long as heaven hangs over the earth.
verses.11:22: For if you keep the commandments that I command you, and do them, to love the Lord your God and to walk in all His ways, clinging to Him,
verses.11:23: the Lord will destroy all these nations before your face, and you will possess them, nations that are greater and stronger than you.
verses.11:24: Every place on which your foot treads will be yours. From the desert and from Lebanon, from the great river Euphrates to the western sea will be your borders.
verses.11:25: No one will stand against you; the Lord your God will put the terror and dread of you upon all the land that you are about to tread on, just as He spoke to you.
verses.11:26: Look, I set in your sight today a blessing and a curse:
verses.11:27: a blessing, if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today;
verses.11:28: a curse, if you do not obey the commandments of the Lord your God, but turn away from the way that I now show you, and walk after foreign gods that you do not know.
verses.11:29: Now when the Lord your God brings you into the land that you are going to inhabit, you shall place the blessing on Mount Gerizim, the curse on Mount Ebal,
verses.11:30: which are across the Jordan, beyond the road that leads toward the setting of the sun, in the land of the Canaanite who lives in the plains opposite Gilgal, which is beside the valley that stretches out and goes far inward.
verses.11:31: For you will cross the Jordan so that you may possess the land that the Lord your God is about to give you, so that you may have and possess it.
verses.11:32: See to it, therefore, that you fulfill the ceremonies and judgments that I will set in your sight today.
verses.12:1: These are the precepts and judgments that you must do in the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, is about to give you, so that you may possess it all the days that you walk upon the ground.
verses.12:2: Overthrow all the places in which the nations that you are about to possess worshiped their gods, on high mountains and hills, and under every leafy tree.
verses.12:3: Tear down their altars and shatter the statues; burn the groves with fire and crush the idols to pieces; destroy their names from those places.
verses.12:4: You shall not do so to the Lord your God;
verses.12:5: but you shall come to the place that the Lord your God will choose from all your tribes, to put His name there and to dwell in it,
verses.12:6: and in that place you shall offer your burnt offerings and sacrifices, tithes and the firstfruits of your hands, and vows and gifts, the firstborn of oxen and sheep.
verses.12:7: And you shall eat there in the sight of the Lord your God, and you and your households shall rejoice in all the things to which you put your hand, in which the Lord your God has blessed you.
verses.12:8: You shall not do there the things that we are doing here today, each one what seems right to himself;
verses.12:9: for up to the present time you have not come to the rest and possession that the Lord your God is about to give you.
verses.12:10: You will cross the Jordan and live in the land that the Lord your God is about to give you, so that you may rest from all enemies on every side, and may live without any fear
verses.12:11: in the place that the Lord your God will choose, so that His name may be in it; to that place you shall bring everything that I command, burnt offerings and sacrifices, and tithes and the firstfruits of your hands, and whatever is choicest among the gifts that you will vow to the Lord.
verses.12:12: There you shall feast before the Lord your God, you and your sons and daughters, male and female servants, and the Levite who resides in your cities; for he has no other share and possession among you.
verses.12:13: Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see,
verses.12:14: but in the place that the Lord will choose in one of your tribes, you shall offer sacrifices, and you shall do whatever I command you.
verses.12:15: But if you wish to eat, and eating meat delights you, slaughter and eat according to the blessing of the Lord your God that He has given you in your cities; whether it is unclean, that is, blemished and weak, or clean, that is, whole and without blemish, which is lawful to offer, you shall eat it just like a roe deer and a stag,
verses.12:16: only without eating the blood, which you shall pour out upon the ground like water.
verses.12:17: You may not eat in your towns the tithe of your grain, wine, and oil, the firstborn of the herds and flocks, and all the things that you vow and wish to offer voluntarily, and the firstfruits of your hands;
verses.12:18: but you shall eat them before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God will choose, you and your son and your daughter, and your male servant and female servant, and the Levite who remains in your cities; and you shall rejoice and be refreshed before the Lord your God in all things to which you stretch out your hand.
verses.12:19: Be careful not to abandon the Levite during all the time that you live in the land.
verses.12:20: When the Lord your God enlarges your borders, just as He spoke to you, and you wish to eat meat that your soul desires,
verses.12:21: and if the place that the Lord your God will choose so that His name may be there is far away, you shall slaughter from the herds and flocks that you have, just as I have commanded you, and you shall eat in your towns, as it pleases you.
verses.12:22: Just as a roe deer and a stag are eaten, so you shall eat them; both the clean and the unclean shall eat together.
verses.12:23: Be careful of this alone, that you do not eat the blood; for their blood is in place of the life, and therefore you must not eat the life with the meat,
verses.12:24: but you shall pour it on the ground like water,
verses.12:25: so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, when you do what is pleasing in the sight of the Lord.
verses.12:26: But the things that you consecrate and vow to the Lord you shall take, and you shall come to the place that the Lord will choose,
verses.12:27: and you shall offer your offerings, the meat and the blood, upon the altar of the Lord your God; the blood of the sacrifices you shall pour on the altar, but you yourself shall eat the meat.
verses.12:28: Observe and hear everything that I command you, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you forever, when you do what is good and pleasing in the sight of the Lord your God.
verses.12:29: When the Lord your God destroys before your face the nations that you will enter to possess, and you possess them and live in their land,
verses.12:30: be careful not to imitate them after they have been overthrown as you enter, and not to inquire into their ceremonies, saying, "Just as these nations worshiped their gods, so I also will worship."
verses.12:31: You shall not do likewise to the Lord your God. For all the abominations that the Lord detests they have done for their gods, offering their sons and daughters and burning them with fire.
verses.13:1: What I command you, do this alone for the Lord; neither add anything nor diminish it.
verses.13:2: If a prophet rises up in your midst, or someone who says that he has seen a dream, and he foretells a sign and a portent,
verses.13:3: and what he spoke comes about, and he says to you, "Let us go and follow foreign gods whom you do not know, and let us serve them,"
verses.13:4: you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer, because the Lord your God is testing you, so that it may become evident whether you love Him or not, with all your heart and with all your soul.
verses.13:5: Follow the Lord your God, and fear Him, and keep His commandments, and listen to His voice; Him you shall serve, and to Him you shall cling.
verses.13:6: But that prophet or fabricator of dreams shall be put to death, because he spoke to turn you away from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, in order to make you stray from the way that the Lord your God commanded you; and you shall remove the evil from your midst.
verses.13:7: If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or daughter, or the wife who is in your embrace, or a friend whom you love as your own soul, wants to persuade you, saying secretly, "Let us go and serve foreign gods," whom you and your fathers do not know,
verses.13:8: of all the nations all around, which are near or far, from the beginning to the end of the earth,
verses.13:9: do not consent to him or listen to him, nor let your eye spare him so that you take pity and conceal him,
verses.13:10: but you shall put him to death immediately; let your hand be upon him first, and afterward let all the people stretch out their hand.
verses.13:11: Overwhelmed with stones, he shall be put to death, because he sought to draw you away from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery,
verses.13:12: so that all Israel, hearing of it, may fear, and never again do anything like this.
verses.13:13: If you hear in one of your cities, which the Lord your God will give you to dwell in, some people saying,
verses.13:14: "Sons of Belial have gone out from your midst and have turned away the inhabitants of their city, and have said, 'Let us go and serve foreign gods whom you do not know,'"
verses.13:15: inquire carefully and diligently; and once the truth of the matter has been thoroughly examined, if you find that what is said is certain and that this abomination has been committed in deed,
verses.13:16: you shall immediately strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, and you shall destroy it and everything that is in it, down to the livestock.
verses.13:17: Also, whatever household goods there may be, you shall gather into the middle of its streets and burn them together with the city itself, so that you consume everything for the Lord your God, and it may be an everlasting mound. It shall not be built again,
verses.13:18: and nothing from that accursed thing shall cling to your hand, so that the Lord may turn away from the anger of His fury, and have mercy on you, and multiply you just as He swore to your fathers,
verses.13:19: when you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, keeping all His precepts that I command you today, so that you do what is pleasing in the sight of the Lord your God.
verses.14:1: Be sons of the Lord your God; you shall not cut yourselves, nor make baldness over a dead person,
verses.14:2: for you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and He has chosen you to be for Him a special people out of all the nations that are upon the earth.
verses.14:3: Do not eat things that are unclean.
verses.14:4: This is the animal that you may eat: the ox, and the sheep, and the goat,
verses.14:5: the stag and the roe deer, the wild ox, the goat-stag, the white-rumped antelope, the oryx, and the giraffe.
verses.14:6: You may eat every animal that splits the hoof into two parts and chews the cud.
verses.14:7: However, of those that chew the cud and do not split the hoof, you must not eat, such as the camel, the hare, and the rock badger; because these chew the cud and do not divide the hoof, they shall be unclean to you.
verses.14:8: The pig also, since it divides the hoof and does not chew the cud, shall be unclean. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall not touch their carcasses.
verses.14:9: These you may eat from all that dwell in the waters: eat those that have fins and scales;
verses.14:10: do not eat those that are without fins and scales, because they are unclean.
verses.14:12: Do not eat the unclean ones: namely, the eagle, and the griffin, and the sea eagle,
verses.14:13: the ixion, and the vulture, and the kite according to its kind;
verses.14:14: and everything of the raven kind;
verses.14:15: and the ostrich, and the owl, and the gull, and the hawk according to its kind;
verses.14:16: the heron, and the swan, and the ibis,
verses.14:17: and the cormorant, the purple swamphen, and the night raven,
verses.14:18: the pelican, and the plover, each in its own kind; also the hoopoe and the bat.
verses.14:19: And everything that creeps and has wings shall be unclean, and it shall not be eaten.
verses.14:21: However, whatever has died of itself, do not eat of it. Give it to the foreigner who is within your gates so that he may eat it, or sell it to him, because you are a holy people of the Lord your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
verses.14:22: You shall set apart a tenth part from all your produce that grows in the land year by year,
verses.14:23: and you shall eat in the sight of the Lord your God, in the place that He chooses so that His name may be called upon in it, the tenth of your grain, and wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herds and your sheep, so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God at all times.
verses.14:24: But when the way is too long, and the place that the Lord your God chooses is too distant, and He has blessed you, and you cannot carry all these things to it,
verses.14:25: you shall sell everything, and convert it into money, and carry it in your hand, and travel to the place that the Lord your God chooses;
verses.14:26: and with that same money you shall buy whatever pleases you, whether from the herds or from the sheep, wine also and strong drink, and everything that your soul desires; and you shall eat before the Lord your God, and you shall feast, you and your household;
verses.14:27: and as for the Levite who is within your gates, take care not to abandon him, because he has no other portion in your possession.
verses.14:28: In the third year you shall set apart another tenth from all things that grow for you at that time, and you shall store it within your doors.
verses.14:29: And the Levite, who has no other portion or possession with you, shall come, and the foreigner, and the orphan, and the widow, who are within your gates, and they shall eat and be filled, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works of your hands that you do.
verses.15:1: In the seventh year you shall grant a remission,
verses.15:2: which shall be observed in this manner. Anyone to whom something is owed by his friend or neighbor and brother shall not be able to demand it back, because it is the Lord's year of remission.
verses.15:3: From a foreigner and a stranger you may exact it; you shall not have the authority to demand it back from a fellow citizen and relative.
verses.15:4: And there shall not be any needy person or beggar at all among you, so that the Lord your God may bless you in the land that He is about to hand over to you for a possession.
verses.15:5: If only you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and keep all things that He has commanded and that I command you today, He will bless you, as He has promised.
verses.15:6: You shall lend to many nations, and you yourself shall borrow from no one. You shall rule over very many nations, and no one shall rule over you.
verses.15:7: If one of your brothers who dwell within the gates of your city, in the land that the Lord your God is about to give you, comes to poverty, you shall not harden your heart nor close your hand,
verses.15:8: but you shall open it to the poor man, and you shall lend him what you see he needs.
verses.15:9: Take care that a wicked thought does not steal into you, and you say in your heart, "The seventh year of remission is drawing near," and you turn your eyes away from your poor brother, unwilling to lend him what he requests, so that he does not cry out against you to the Lord, and it becomes a sin for you.
verses.15:10: Rather, you shall give to him, nor shall you do anything craftily in relieving his needs, so that the Lord your God may bless you at all times, and in everything to which you put your hand.
verses.15:11: The poor will not be lacking in the land of your dwelling; therefore I command you to open your hand to your needy and poor brother who lives with you in the land.
verses.15:12: When your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold to you and has served you for six years, in the seventh year you shall send him away free;
verses.15:13: and the one to whom you have granted freedom you shall by no means allow to go away empty-handed;
verses.15:14: but you shall give provisions for the journey from your flocks, and from your threshing floor, and your winepress, with which the Lord your God has blessed you.
verses.15:15: Remember that you yourself also served in the land of Egypt, and that the Lord your God freed you, and therefore I now command you.
verses.15:16: But if he says, "I do not want to leave," because he loves you and your household, and feels that he is well off with you,
verses.15:17: you shall take an awl and pierce his ear at the door of your house, and he shall serve you forever. To a female servant also you shall do likewise.
verses.15:18: Do not turn your eyes away from them when you send them away free, because according to the wages of a hired laborer he has served you for six years, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works that you do.
verses.15:19: Of the firstborn that are born in your herds and in your sheep, whatever is of the male sex you shall consecrate to the Lord your God. You shall not work with the firstborn of the ox, and you shall not shear the firstborn of the sheep.
verses.15:20: In the sight of the Lord your God you shall eat them year by year in the place that the Lord chooses, you and your household.
verses.15:21: But if it has a blemish, or is lame, or blind, or deformed or weak in any part, it shall not be sacrificed to the Lord your God;
verses.15:22: but you shall eat it within the gates of your city; both the clean and the unclean alike shall eat of them, like the roe deer and the stag.
verses.15:23: This alone you shall observe, that you do not eat their blood, but you shall pour it out on the ground like water.
verses.16:1: Observe the month of new produce, and the first of the spring season, so that you may keep the Passover to the Lord your God, because in that month the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
verses.16:2: And you shall sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God from the sheep and from the cattle, in the place that the Lord your God will choose, so that His name may dwell there.
verses.16:3: You shall not eat leavened bread with it; for seven days you shall eat bread of affliction without leaven, because you came out of Egypt in fear, so that you may remember the day of your departure from Egypt all the days of your life.
verses.16:4: No leaven shall appear within all your borders for seven days, and nothing of the flesh of what was sacrificed in the evening on the first day shall remain until morning.
verses.16:5: You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any of your cities that the Lord your God is about to give you,
verses.16:6: but in the place that the Lord your God will choose, so that His name may dwell there. You shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening at the setting of the sun, when you came out of Egypt.
verses.16:7: And you shall cook and eat it in the place that the Lord your God will choose, and rising in the morning, you shall go to your tents.
verses.16:8: For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day, because it is an assembly of the Lord your God, you shall do no work.
verses.16:9: You shall count seven weeks for yourself from the day on which you put the sickle to the standing grain.
verses.16:10: And you shall celebrate the feast day of Weeks to the Lord your God, with a voluntary offering of your hand, which you shall offer according to the blessing of the Lord your God,
verses.16:11: and you shall feast before the Lord your God, you, your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and the Levite who is within your gates, the foreigner and the orphan and the widow who dwell with you, in the place that the Lord your God will choose, so that His name may dwell there.
verses.16:12: And you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and you shall keep and do the things that have been commanded.
verses.16:13: You shall also celebrate the solemn feast of Tabernacles for seven days, when you have gathered your produce from the threshing floor and the winepress,
verses.16:14: and you shall feast in your festival, you, your son and daughter, your male servant and female servant, also the Levite and the foreigner, the orphan and the widow who are within your gates.
verses.16:15: For seven days you shall celebrate feasts to the Lord your God in the place that the Lord will choose; and the Lord your God will bless you in all your produce and in every work of your hands, and you will be in gladness.
verses.16:16: Three times a year every male of yours shall appear in the sight of the Lord your God in the place that He will choose: at the solemn feast of Unleavened Bread, at the solemn feast of Weeks, and at the solemn feast of Tabernacles. He shall not appear before the Lord empty,
verses.16:17: but each one shall offer in accordance with what he has, according to the blessing of the Lord his God that He has given him.
verses.16:18: You shall appoint judges and officials in all your gates that the Lord your God will give you, throughout each of your tribes, so that they may judge the people with just judgment,
verses.16:19: and not turn aside to either side. You shall not show partiality or accept bribes, because bribes blind the eyes of the wise and change the words of the righteous.
verses.16:20: You shall justly pursue what is just, so that you may live and possess the land that the Lord your God will give you.
verses.16:21: You shall not plant a grove or any tree beside the altar of the Lord your God.
verses.16:22: Neither shall you make for yourself nor set up a statue: things that the Lord your God hates.
verses.17:1: You shall not sacrifice to the Lord your God a sheep or an ox in which there is a blemish or any kind of defect, because it is an abomination to the Lord your God.
verses.17:2: When a man or a woman is found among you within one of your gates that the Lord your God will give you, who does evil in the sight of the Lord your God and transgresses His covenant,
verses.17:3: so as to go and serve foreign gods and worship them, the sun and the moon, and all the host of heaven, which I did not command,
verses.17:4: and this is reported to you, and hearing it, you inquire diligently and find it to be true, and an abomination has been committed in Israel,
verses.17:5: you shall bring out the man and the woman who committed a most wicked deed to the gates of your city, and they shall be overwhelmed with stones.
verses.17:6: By the mouth of two or three witnesses, the one who is to be put to death shall perish. Let no one be killed when one person gives testimony against him.
verses.17:7: The hand of the witnesses shall first put him to death, and the hand of the rest of the people shall be put forth last, so that you may remove the evil from your midst.
verses.17:8: If you perceive that a judgment before you is difficult and uncertain, between blood and blood, case and case, leprosy and leprosy, and you see that the words of the judges within your gates vary, rise and go up to the place that the Lord your God will choose.
verses.17:9: And you shall come to the priests of the Levitical lineage and to the judge who is there at that time; and you shall inquire of them, and they will declare to you the truth of the judgment.
verses.17:10: And you shall do whatever those who preside over the place that the Lord will choose say and teach you
verses.17:11: according to His law, and you shall follow their decision, and you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.17:12: As for the one who acts proudly, unwilling to obey the command of the priest who ministers at that time to the Lord your God, and the decree of the judge, that man shall die, and you shall remove the evil from Israel;
verses.17:13: and all the people, hearing this, will fear, so that no one from then on may swell with pride.
verses.17:14: When you have entered the land that the Lord your God will give you, and have possessed it and dwelt in it, and say, "I will appoint a king over myself, just as all the nations all around have,"
verses.17:15: you shall appoint the one whom the Lord your God will choose from the number of your brothers. You may not make a man of another nation king, who is not your brother.
verses.17:16: And when he has been appointed, he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor lead the people back to Egypt, lifted up by the number of cavalry, especially since the Lord has commanded you that you should never again return by that same way.
verses.17:17: He shall not have very many wives, who might entice his mind, nor immense weights of silver and gold.
verses.17:18: Now after he has sat on the throne of his kingdom, he shall write out for himself the Deuteronomy of this law on a scroll, receiving the copy from the priests of the Levitical tribe,
verses.17:19: and he shall keep it with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord his God and to keep His words and ceremonies that have been commanded in the law.
verses.17:20: And let his heart not be lifted up in pride over his brothers, nor let him turn aside to the right side or the left, so that he and his sons may reign for a long time over Israel.
verses.18:1: The priests and the Levites, and all who are of the same tribe, shall have no portion and inheritance with the rest of Israel, because they shall eat the sacrifices of the Lord and His offerings,
verses.18:2: and they shall receive nothing else from the possession of their brothers; for the Lord Himself is their inheritance, just as He spoke to them.
verses.18:3: This shall be the right of the priests from the people, and from those who offer sacrificial victims: whether they sacrifice an ox or a sheep, they shall give to the priest the shoulder and the stomach;
verses.18:4: the firstfruits of grain, wine, and oil, and a portion of the wool from the shearing of the sheep.
verses.18:5: For the Lord your God has chosen him out of all your tribes to stand and minister to the name of the Lord, he and his sons forever.
verses.18:6: If a Levite goes out from one of your cities out of all Israel in which he dwells, and wishes to come, longing for the place that the Lord will choose,
verses.18:7: he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, just like all his brothers the Levites who will stand at that time before the Lord.
