verses.18:8: He shall receive the same portion of food as the others, except for what is owed to him in his own city by paternal succession.
verses.18:9: When you have entered the land that the Lord your God will give you, be careful that you do not wish to imitate the abominations of those nations.
verses.18:10: Let there not be found among you anyone who purifies his son or daughter, leading them through fire, or who consults soothsayers and observes dreams and auguries, nor let there be a sorcerer,
verses.18:11: nor an enchanter, nor anyone who consults mediums or diviners, or seeks the truth from the dead.
verses.18:12: For the Lord abhors all these things, and because of crimes of this sort He will destroy them at your entrance.
verses.18:13: You shall be perfect and without blemish with the Lord your God.
verses.18:14: These nations, whose land you will possess, listen to augurs and diviners; but you have been instructed otherwise by the Lord your God.
verses.18:15: A prophet from your nation and from your brothers, like me, the Lord your God will raise up for you; to him you shall listen,
verses.18:16: just as you asked of the Lord your God at Horeb, when the assembly was gathered together, and you said, "I will no longer hear the voice of the Lord my God, and I will no longer see this exceedingly great fire, so that I do not die."
verses.18:17: And the Lord said to me, "They have spoken all things well.
verses.18:18: I will raise up for them a prophet from the midst of their brothers, like you, and I will put My words in his mouth, and he will speak to them everything that I command him.
verses.18:19: And as for the one who is unwilling to listen to his words that he will speak in My name, I Myself will be the avenger.
verses.18:20: But the prophet who, corrupted by arrogance, chooses to speak in My name things that I did not command him to say, or by the name of foreign gods, shall be put to death."
verses.18:21: And if in silent thought you reply, "How can I discern the word that the Lord has not spoken?"
verses.18:22: you shall have this sign: whatever that prophet has foretold in the name of the Lord and it does not come about, this the Lord has not spoken, but the prophet has fabricated it through the swelling of his mind, and therefore you shall not fear him.
verses.19:1: When the Lord your God has destroyed the nations whose land He is about to hand over to you, and you have possessed it and lived in its cities and in its houses,
verses.19:2: you shall set apart three cities for yourself in the midst of the land that the Lord your God will give you as a possession,
verses.19:3: carefully preparing the road; and you shall divide the entire territory of your land equally into three parts, so that the one who is a fugitive on account of homicide may have nearby a place to which he can escape.
verses.19:4: This shall be the law of the fleeing killer whose life is to be preserved: the one who strikes his neighbor unknowingly, and who is proved to have held no hatred against him yesterday and the day before yesterday,
verses.19:5: but to have gone with him simply into the forest to cut wood, and in the cutting down of the wood the axe flies from his hand, and the iron, slipping off the handle, strikes his friend and kills him: this man shall flee to one of the aforementioned cities and live,
verses.19:6: so that the near relative of the one whose blood was shed may not perhaps, goaded by grief, pursue and seize him if the road is too long, and strike down his life, though he is not liable to death, because he is shown to have held no prior hatred against the one who was killed.
verses.19:7: Therefore I command you to divide off three cities at equal distance from one another.
verses.19:8: Now when the Lord your God has enlarged your borders, just as He swore to your fathers, and has given you all the land that He promised them
verses.19:9: (if indeed you keep His commandments and do what I command you today, to love the Lord your God and to walk in His ways at all times), you shall add for yourself three other cities, and you shall double the number of the three aforementioned cities,
verses.19:10: so that innocent blood may not be shed in the midst of the land that the Lord your God will give you to possess, and so that you may not be guilty of blood.
verses.19:11: But if anyone, hating his neighbor, lies in wait for his life, and rises up and strikes him so that he dies, and flees to one of the aforementioned cities,
verses.19:12: the elders of that city shall send and seize him from the place of refuge, and hand him over into the hand of the near relative of the one whose blood was shed, and he shall die.
verses.19:13: You shall show him no pity, and you shall remove innocent blood from Israel, so that it may go well with you.
verses.19:14: You shall not take up and move the boundary markers of your neighbor, which predecessors fixed in your possession, which the Lord your God will give you in the land that you receive to possess.
verses.19:15: A single witness shall not stand against anyone, whatever that sin and crime may be; rather, every word shall stand by the mouth of two or three witnesses.
verses.19:16: If a lying witness stands against a man, accusing him of transgression,
verses.19:17: both of those whose case it is shall stand before the Lord in the presence of the priests and the judges who shall be in those days.
verses.19:18: And when, investigating most diligently, they find that the false witness has spoken a lie against his brother,
verses.19:19: they shall repay him just as he planned to do to his brother, and you shall remove the evil from your midst,
verses.19:20: so that the rest, hearing of it, may have fear, and by no means dare to do such things.
verses.19:21: You shall show him no pity, but you shall exact life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
verses.20:1: If you go out to war against your enemies, and see cavalry and chariots, and a greater multitude of the opposing army than you have, you shall not fear them, because the Lord your God is with you, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
verses.20:2: Now when the battle is already drawing near, the priest shall stand before the battle line and speak to the people in this way:
verses.20:3: "Hear, Israel: today you are joining battle against your enemies. Let your heart not be terrified; do not be afraid, do not give way, and do not dread them,
verses.20:4: because the Lord your God is in your midst, and He will fight for you against the adversaries, to rescue you from danger."
verses.20:5: The commanders also shall proclaim through each troop, with the army listening: "Who is the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, so that he may not perhaps die in war and another dedicate it.
verses.20:6: Who is the man who has planted a vineyard and has not yet made it common, from which all are permitted to eat? Let him go and return to his house, so that he may not perhaps die in war and another man perform his duty.
verses.20:7: Who is the man who has betrothed a wife and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, so that he may not perhaps die in war and another man take her."
verses.20:8: When these things have been said, they shall add the rest and speak to the people: "Who is a fearful man and of a trembling heart? Let him go and return to his house, so that he may not make the hearts of his brothers tremble, just as he himself is terrified with fear."
verses.20:9: And when the commanders of the army have fallen silent and made an end of speaking, each one shall prepare his own battle formations for fighting.
verses.20:10: Whenever you approach to storm a city, you shall first offer it peace.
verses.20:11: If it accepts and opens the gates to you, all the people who are in it shall be saved and shall serve you under tribute.
verses.20:12: But if it is unwilling to enter into a covenant and begins war against you, you shall attack it.
verses.20:13: And when the Lord your God hands it over into your hand, you shall strike down everything in it that is of the male sex with the edge of the sword,
verses.20:14: except the women and young children, the livestock, and the rest of the things that are in the city. You shall divide all the plunder for the army, and you shall eat from the spoils of your enemies, which the Lord your God will give you.
verses.20:15: So you shall do to all the cities that are very far from you, and are not of these cities that you are about to receive as a possession.
verses.20:16: But of these cities that will be given to you, you shall permit no one at all to live;
verses.20:17: rather, you shall kill them with the edge of the sword, namely the Hittite and the Amorite and the Canaanite, the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, just as the Lord your God has commanded you,
verses.20:18: so that they may not perhaps teach you to do all the abominations that they themselves have practiced for their gods, and so that you may not sin against the Lord your God.
verses.20:19: When you besiege a city for a long time and surround it with fortifications in order to storm it, you shall not cut down trees from which one can eat, nor should you lay waste the region all around with axes, for it is a tree, and not a man, nor can it increase the number of those fighting against you.
verses.20:20: But if any trees are not fruit-bearing, but wild and suited for other uses, cut them down and build siege engines until you capture the city that fights against you.
verses.21:1: When the corpse of a killed man is found in the land that the Lord your God is about to give you, and the one guilty of the killing is unknown,
verses.21:2: your elders and judges shall go out and measure from the place of the corpse the distances to each of the cities all around;
verses.21:3: and whichever city they determine to be nearer than the rest, the elders of that city shall take a heifer from the herd that has not pulled a yoke nor cut the earth with a plowshare,
verses.21:4: and they shall lead her to a rough and rocky valley that has never been plowed nor received seed, and in it they shall cut the neck of the heifer.
verses.21:5: And the priests, the sons of Levi, shall come forward, whom the Lord your God has chosen to minister to Him and to bless in His name, and at their word every matter and whatever is clean or unclean shall be judged.
verses.21:6: And the elders of that city shall come to the one who was killed, and shall wash their hands over the heifer that was struck down in the valley,
verses.21:7: and shall say: "Our hands have not shed this blood, nor have our eyes seen it.
verses.21:8: Be merciful to Your people Israel, whom You have redeemed, Lord, and do not reckon innocent blood in the midst of Your people Israel." And the guilt of blood shall be removed from them,
verses.21:9: and you shall be free from the blood of the innocent that was poured out, when you have done what the Lord has commanded.
verses.21:10: If you go out to battle against your enemies, and the Lord your God hands them over into your hand, and you lead them away as captives,
verses.21:11: and you see among the number of the captives a beautiful woman, and fall in love with her, and wish to have her as a wife,
verses.21:12: you shall bring her into your house; she shall shave her hair and trim her nails,
verses.21:13: and lay aside the garment in which she was captured; and sitting in your house, she shall weep for her father and her mother for one month; and afterward you shall go in to her and sleep with her, and she shall be your wife.
verses.21:14: But if afterward she does not please your mind, you shall send her away free; you shall not be able to sell her for money, nor oppress her by power, because you have humbled her.
verses.21:15: If a man has two wives, one loved and the other hated, and they have borne children by him, and the son of the hated one is the firstborn,
verses.21:16: and he wishes to divide his property among his sons, he shall not be able to make the son of the loved one the firstborn and prefer him to the son of the hated one;
verses.21:17: rather, he shall acknowledge the son of the hated one as the firstborn, and shall give him double of all the things that he possesses; for this one is the beginning of his children, and to him the rights of the firstborn are due.
verses.21:18: If a man fathers a stubborn and insolent son who does not listen to the command of his father or mother, and though disciplined scorns to obey,
verses.21:19: they shall seize him and lead him to the elders of that city and to the gate of judgment,
verses.21:20: and shall say to them: "This son of ours is insolent and stubborn; he scorns to listen to our warnings; he devotes himself to carousing, and to debauchery and banquets."
verses.21:21: The people of the city shall overwhelm him with stones, and he shall die, so that you may remove the evil from your midst, and all Israel, hearing of it, may be terrified.
verses.21:22: When a man commits a sin that must be punished with death, and having been sentenced to death is hung on a gibbet,
verses.21:23: his corpse shall not remain on the wood, but shall be buried on the same day, because the one who hangs on wood is cursed by God; and by no means shall you contaminate your land, which the Lord your God will give you as a possession.
verses.22:1: You shall not see your brother's ox or sheep straying and pass by, but you shall lead it back to your brother,
verses.22:2: even if your brother is not near and you do not know him; you shall lead them into your house, and they shall remain with you until your brother searches for them and receives them back.
verses.22:3: You shall do likewise with a donkey, and with a garment, and with anything of your brother's that has been lost; if you find it, do not neglect it as though it belonged to another.
verses.22:4: If you see your brother's donkey or ox fallen on the road, you shall not disregard it, but you shall lift it up with him.
verses.22:5: A woman shall not put on a man's clothing, nor shall a man use a woman's clothing, for the one who does these things is abominable before God.
verses.22:6: If, while walking along the road, you find a bird's nest in a tree or on the ground, with the mother brooding above the chicks or the eggs, you shall not keep her with the young,
verses.22:7: but you shall allow her to go away, keeping the captured young, so that it may go well for you and you may live a long time.
verses.22:8: When you build a new house, you shall make a wall all around the roof, so that blood may not be shed in your house and you may not be guilty if someone slips and plunges headlong.
verses.22:9: You shall not sow your vineyard with another seed, so that both the crop that you have sown and what grows from the vineyard may not be sanctified together.
verses.22:10: You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together.
verses.22:11: You shall not put on a garment that is woven together of wool and linen.
verses.22:12: You shall make cords on the fringes at the four corners of your cloak, with which you cover yourself.
verses.22:13: If a man takes a wife and afterward hates her,
verses.22:14: and looks for pretexts by which he may send her away, bringing a very bad name against her, and says, "I took this woman as a wife, and having gone in to her, I did not find her a virgin,"
verses.22:15: then her father and her mother shall take her and bring with them the signs of her virginity to the elders of the city who are at the gate,
verses.22:16: and the father shall say, "I gave my daughter to this man as a wife, and because he hates her,
verses.22:17: he puts a very bad name upon her, so as to say, 'I did not find your daughter a virgin.' And look, these are the signs of my daughter's virginity." They shall spread out the garment before the elders of the city,
verses.22:18: and the elders of that city shall seize the man and flog him,
verses.22:19: condemning him besides to one hundred shekels of silver, which he shall give to the father of the young woman, because he spread a very bad name over a virgin of Israel; and he shall have her as his wife, and he will not be able to send her away all the days of his life.
verses.22:20: But if what he brings against her is true, and virginity is not found in the young woman,
verses.22:21: they shall cast her out beyond the doors of her father's house, and the men of that city shall overwhelm her with stones, and she shall die, because she committed an outrage in Israel by committing fornication in her father's house; and you shall remove the evil from your midst.
verses.22:22: If a man sleeps with another's wife, both of them shall die, that is, the adulterer and the adulteress; and you shall remove the evil from Israel.
verses.22:23: If a man has betrothed a young woman who is a virgin, and someone finds her in the city and lies with her,
verses.22:24: you shall bring both of them out to the gate of that city, and they shall be overwhelmed with stones: the young woman, because she did not cry out while she was in the city; the man, because he humiliated his neighbor's wife; and you shall remove the evil from your midst.
verses.22:25: But if in the field a man finds a young woman who is betrothed, and seizing her, lies with her, he alone shall die;
verses.22:26: the young woman shall suffer nothing, nor is she guilty of death, for just as a robber rises up against his brother and takes his life, so also has the young woman suffered.
verses.22:27: She was alone in the field; she cried out, and no one was present to rescue her.
verses.22:28: If a man finds a young woman who is a virgin, who has no betrothed, and seizing her, lies with her, and the matter comes to judgment,
verses.22:29: the one who slept with her shall give fifty shekels of silver to the father of the young woman, and he shall have her as his wife, because he humiliated her; he will not be able to send her away all the days of his life.
verses.23:1: A man shall not take his father's wife, nor shall he uncover his covering.
verses.23:2: A eunuch with crushed or amputated testicles and a severed male member shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
verses.23:3: A mamzer, that is, one born of a prostitute, shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord, up to the tenth generation.
verses.23:4: An Ammonite and a Moabite, even after the tenth generation, shall not enter the assembly of the Lord forever,
verses.23:5: because they were unwilling to meet you with bread and water on the road when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam, the son of Beor, from Mesopotamia of Syria, so that he might curse you;
verses.23:6: and the Lord your God was unwilling to listen to Balaam, and He turned his curse into a blessing for you, because He loved you.
verses.23:7: You shall not make peace with them, nor seek good things for them all the days of your life forever.
verses.23:8: You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother, nor an Egyptian, for you were a resident alien in his land.
verses.23:9: Those who are born from them shall enter into the assembly of the Lord in the third generation.
verses.23:10: When you go out against your enemies into battle, you shall guard yourself from every evil thing.
verses.23:11: If there is a man among you who has been defiled by a nocturnal dream, he shall go outside the camp,
verses.23:12: and he shall not return before he washes himself with water toward evening, and after the setting of the sun he shall go back into the camp.
verses.23:13: You shall have a place outside the camp to which you may go out for the necessities of nature,
verses.23:14: carrying a stake in your belt; and when you sit down, you shall dig all around, and with the dug-up earth you shall cover
verses.23:15: where you uncovered yourself; for the Lord your God walks in the midst of the camp to rescue you and to hand over your enemies to you; and let your camp be holy, and let nothing foul appear in it, so that He may not abandon you.
verses.23:16: You shall not hand over to his master a slave who has fled to you for refuge.
verses.23:17: He shall dwell with you in the place that pleases him, and he shall rest in one of your cities; do not grieve him.
verses.23:18: There shall be no prostitute from the daughters of Israel, nor any fornicator from the sons of Israel.
verses.23:19: You shall not offer the wages of a prostitute nor the price of a dog in the house of the Lord your God, whatever it is that you have vowed, for both are an abomination before the Lord your God.
verses.23:20: You shall not lend money, nor produce, nor any other thing at interest to your brother,
verses.23:21: but to a foreigner. To your brother, however, you shall lend without interest what he needs, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all your work in the land that you are entering to possess.
verses.23:22: When you make a vow to the Lord your God, you shall not be slow to pay it, for the Lord your God will require it, and if you delay, it will be counted to you as sin.
verses.23:23: If you are unwilling to promise, you will be without sin.
verses.23:24: But what has once gone out from your lips you shall observe and do, just as you promised to the Lord your God and spoke of your own free will and with your own mouth.
verses.23:25: If you enter into your friend's standing grain, you may break off the heads of grain and rub them with your hand, but you shall not reap with a sickle.
verses.23:26: Having entered your neighbor's vineyard, eat grapes as much as pleases you, but do not carry any outside with you.
verses.24:1: If a man takes a wife and has her, and she does not find favor before his eyes because of some indecency, he shall write a document of divorce and place it in her hand, and send her away from his house.
verses.24:2: And when, after going out, she marries another husband,
verses.24:3: and he also hates her, and gives her a document of divorce, and sends her away from his house, or indeed dies,
verses.24:4: the former husband will not be able to take her back as a wife, because she has been defiled and has become abominable before the Lord, so that you do not cause your land to sin, which the Lord your God delivers to you to possess.
verses.24:5: When a man has recently taken a wife, he shall not go out to war, nor shall any public obligation be imposed on him, but he shall remain free without blame at his own home, so that for one year he may rejoice with his wife.
verses.24:6: You shall not take the lower and the upper millstone as a pledge, because he has pledged his own life to you.
verses.24:7: If a man is caught enticing away his brother from the sons of Israel, and after selling him receives the price, he shall be put to death, and you shall remove the evil from your midst.
verses.24:8: Watch carefully so that you do not incur the plague of leprosy, but you shall do whatever the priests of the Levitical lineage teach you, according to what I commanded them, and fulfill it diligently.
verses.24:9: Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam on the way when you were coming out of Egypt.
verses.24:10: When you claim back from your neighbor anything that he owes you, you shall not enter his house to take away a pledge,
verses.24:11: but you shall stand outside, and he shall bring out to you what he has.
verses.24:12: But if he is poor, the pledge shall not stay overnight with you,
verses.24:13: but you shall immediately return it to him before sunset, so that, sleeping in his own garment, he may bless you, and you may have righteousness before the Lord your God.
verses.24:14: You shall not deny the wages of your needy and poor brother, or of the sojourner who resides with you in the land and is within your gates,
verses.24:15: but on the same day you shall pay him the price of his labor before sunset, because he is poor and sustains his life by it; otherwise he will cry out against you to the Lord, and it will be counted to you as sin.
verses.24:16: Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, nor sons for fathers, but each one shall die for his own sin.
verses.24:17: You shall not pervert the justice of the sojourner and the orphan, nor shall you take away a widow's garment as a pledge.
verses.24:18: Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the Lord your God rescued you from there. Therefore I command you to do this thing.
verses.24:19: When you harvest the crop in your field and, forgetting, leave a sheaf, you shall not turn back to pick it up, but you shall allow the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow to take it away, so that the Lord your God may bless you in every work of your hands.
verses.24:20: If you gather the fruit of olive trees, whatever remains on the trees you shall not turn back to gather, but you shall leave it for the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow.
verses.24:21: If you gather the vintage of your vineyard, you shall not gather the remaining clusters, but they shall go to the use of the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow.
verses.24:22: Remember that you also were a slave in Egypt, and therefore I command you to do this thing.
verses.25:1: If there is a dispute between some people and they appeal to the judges, to the one whom they discern to be righteous they shall give the palm of righteousness; the one who is wicked they shall condemn for wickedness.
verses.25:2: But if they see that the one who has sinned is deserving of blows, they shall lay him down and have him beaten in their presence. According to the measure of the sin shall also be the limit of the blows,
verses.25:3: provided only that they do not exceed the number of forty, so that your brother does not depart shamefully torn before your eyes.
verses.25:4: You shall not bind the mouth of the ox treading out your produce on the threshing floor.
verses.25:5: When brothers live together, and one of them dies without children, the wife of the deceased shall not marry another, but his brother shall take her and raise up the seed of his brother,
verses.25:6: and he shall call the firstborn son from her by his name, so that his name may not be blotted out from Israel.
verses.25:7: But if he is unwilling to take his brother's wife, who is owed to him by law, the woman shall go to the gate of the city and appeal to the elders, and say, "My husband's brother is unwilling to raise up his brother's name in Israel, or to take me as a wife."
verses.25:8: And immediately they shall have him summoned and question him. If he answers, "I am unwilling to take her as a wife,"
verses.25:9: the woman shall approach him before the elders, and take the sandal off his foot, and spit in his face, and say, "So it shall be done to the man who does not build his brother's house."
verses.25:10: And his name shall be called in Israel, "The House of the Unshod."
verses.25:11: If two men have a quarrel between themselves, and one begins to fight against the other, and the wife of one of them, wanting to rescue her husband from the hand of the stronger one, stretches out her hand and seizes his private parts,
verses.25:12: you shall cut off her hand, nor shall you be moved by any mercy toward her.
verses.25:13: You shall not have differing weights in a bag, a larger and a smaller,
verses.25:14: nor shall there be in your house a larger and a smaller measure.
verses.25:15: You shall have a just and true weight, and you shall have an equal and true measure, so that you may live a long time upon the land that the Lord your God gives you.
verses.25:16: For your Lord abhors the one who does these things and recoils from all injustice.
verses.25:17: Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you were coming out of Egypt,
verses.25:18: how he met you and cut down the hindmost of your column, who were lingering behind weary, when you were worn out by hunger and toil, and he did not fear God.
verses.25:19: Therefore, when the Lord your God gives you rest and subjects all the surrounding nations in the land that He has promised to you, you shall blot out his name from under heaven. Take care that you do not forget.
verses.26:1: And when you enter the land that the Lord your God is about to give you to possess, and you obtain it and dwell in it,
verses.26:2: you shall take the firstfruits from all your produce and place them in a basket, and go to the place that the Lord your God chooses, so that His name may be called upon there,
verses.26:3: and you shall approach the priest who will be in those days, and say to him, "I profess today before the Lord your God that I have entered the land concerning which He swore to our fathers that He would give it to us."
verses.26:4: And the priest, receiving the basket from your hand, shall place it before the altar of the Lord your God,
verses.26:5: and you shall speak in the sight of the Lord your God, "A Syrian was persecuting my father, who went down into Egypt and sojourned there in very small number, and grew into a great and mighty nation, and of countless multitude.
verses.26:6: And the Egyptians afflicted us and persecuted us, imposing very heavy burdens,
verses.26:7: and we cried out to the Lord, the God of our fathers, who heard us and looked upon our lowliness, toil, and distress,
verses.26:8: and brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, with immense terror, with signs and wonders,
verses.26:9: and brought us into this place, and delivered to us a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.26:10: And therefore now I offer the firstfruits of the produce of the land that the Lord has given to me." And you shall leave them in the sight of the Lord your God; and having worshiped the Lord your God,
verses.26:11: you shall then feast on all the good things that the Lord your God has given to you and to your house, you and the Levite and the sojourner who is with you.
verses.26:12: When you have completed the tithe of all your produce in the third year of tithes, you shall give it to the Levite, the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow, so that they may eat within your gates and be filled,
verses.26:13: and you shall speak in the sight of the Lord your God, "I have removed what has been sanctified from my house and have given it to the Levite, the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow, just as You commanded me; I have not passed over Your commandments, nor have I forgotten Your command.
verses.26:14: I have not eaten of them in my mourning, nor have I set them apart in any uncleanness, nor have I spent anything from them on a funeral matter. I have obeyed the voice of the Lord my God, and have done all things just as You commanded me.
verses.26:15: Look down from Your sanctuary and from the lofty dwelling place of the heavens, and bless Your people Israel and the land that You have given to us, just as You swore to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey."
verses.26:16: Today the Lord your God has commanded you to do these commandments and judgments, and to keep and fulfill them with all your heart and with all your soul.
verses.26:17: You have chosen the Lord today to be God to you, and that you may walk in His ways, and keep His ceremonies, commandments, and judgments, and obey His command.
verses.26:18: And the Lord has chosen you today so that you may be a special people to Him, just as He spoke to you, and that you may keep all His precepts,
verses.26:19: and that He may make you higher than all the nations that He has created, for His praise, name, and glory, so that you may be a holy people of the Lord your God, just as He spoke.
verses.27:1: And Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, "Observe every commandment that I command you today.
verses.27:2: And when you have crossed the Jordan into the land that the Lord your God will give you, you will set up huge stones and smooth them over with lime,
verses.27:3: so that you may be able to write on them all the words of this law, once the Jordan has been crossed, so that you may enter the land that the Lord your God will give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as He swore to your fathers.
verses.27:4: Therefore, when you have crossed the Jordan, set up on Mount Ebal the stones that I command you today, and you will smooth them over with lime;
verses.27:5: and you will build an altar there to the Lord your God of stones that iron has not touched,
verses.27:6: and of unshaped and unpolished rocks; and you will offer on it burnt offerings to the Lord your God,
verses.27:7: and you will sacrifice peace offerings, and you will eat there and feast before the Lord your God.
verses.27:8: And you will write on the stones all the words of this law plainly and clearly."
verses.27:9: And Moses and the priests of Levitical lineage said to all Israel, "Pay attention and listen, Israel: today you have become the people of the Lord your God;
verses.27:10: you will listen to His voice, and you will carry out the commandments and righteous decrees that I command you."
verses.27:11: And Moses commanded the people on that day, saying,
verses.27:12: "These will stand to bless the people on Mount Gerizim, once the Jordan has been crossed: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
verses.27:13: And on the opposite side, these will stand to curse on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, and Asher, and Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
verses.27:14: And the Levites will declare and say to all the men of Israel with a loud voice:
verses.27:15: 'Cursed is the man who makes a carved and cast image, an abomination to the Lord, the work of the hands of craftsmen, and will set it in a hidden place.' And all the people will answer and say, 'Amen.'
verses.27:16: 'Cursed is the one who does not honor his father and mother.' And all the people will say, 'Amen.'
verses.27:17: 'Cursed is the one who moves the boundaries of his neighbor.' And all the people will say, 'Amen.'
verses.27:18: 'Cursed is the one who causes a blind man to go astray on the road.' And all the people will say, 'Amen.'
verses.27:19: 'Cursed is the one who perverts the justice of the stranger, the orphan, and the widow.' And all the people will say, 'Amen.'
verses.27:20: 'Cursed is the one who sleeps with the wife of his father and uncovers the covering of his bed.' And all the people will say, 'Amen.'
verses.27:21: 'Cursed is the one who sleeps with any animal.' And all the people will say, 'Amen.'
verses.27:22: 'Cursed is the one who sleeps with his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother.' And all the people will say, 'Amen.'
verses.27:23: 'Cursed is the one who sleeps with his mother-in-law.' And all the people will say, 'Amen.'
verses.27:24: 'Cursed is the one who secretly strikes down his neighbor.' And all the people will say, 'Amen.'
verses.27:25: 'Cursed is the one who accepts bribes to strike down a life of innocent blood.' And all the people will say, 'Amen.'
verses.27:26: 'Cursed is the one who does not remain in the words of this law, and does not fulfill them in deed.' And all the people will say, 'Amen.'"
verses.28:1: Now if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to do and keep all His commandments which I command you today, the Lord your God will make you higher than all the nations that dwell on the earth.
verses.28:2: And all these blessings will come upon you and take hold of you, if only you listen to His precepts.
verses.28:3: Blessed are you in the city, and blessed in the field.
verses.28:4: Blessed is the fruit of your womb, and the fruit of your land, and the fruit of your livestock, the herds of your cattle, and the folds of your sheep.
verses.28:5: Blessed are your granaries, and blessed are your remnants.
verses.28:6: Blessed will you be coming in and going out.
verses.28:7: The Lord will cause your enemies who rise up against you to fall in your sight; by one way they will come against you, and by seven they will flee from your face.
verses.28:8: The Lord will send forth a blessing upon your storerooms and upon all the works of your hands, and He will bless you in the land that you will receive.
verses.28:9: The Lord will raise you up for Himself as a holy people, just as He swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the Lord your God and walk in His ways.
verses.28:10: And all the peoples of the lands will see that the name of the Lord has been invoked upon you, and they will fear you.
verses.28:11: The Lord will make you abound in all good things: in the fruit of your womb, and in the fruit of your livestock, in the fruit of your land, which the Lord swore to your fathers that He would give you.
verses.28:12: The Lord will open His best treasury, the sky, to grant rain to your land in its season, and He will bless all the works of your hands. And you will lend to many nations, and you yourself will take a loan from no one.
verses.28:13: The Lord will establish you as the head and not as the tail, and you will always be above and not beneath, if only you listen to the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you today, and keep and do them,
verses.28:14: and do not turn aside from them to the right or to the left, nor follow foreign gods, nor worship them.
verses.28:15: But if you are unwilling to listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all His commandments and ceremonies which I command you today, all these curses will come upon you and take hold of you.
verses.28:16: Cursed will you be in the city, cursed in the field.
verses.28:17: Cursed is your granary, and cursed are your remnants.
verses.28:18: Cursed is the fruit of your womb, and the fruit of your land, the herds of your oxen, and the flocks of your sheep.
verses.28:19: Cursed will you be coming in, and cursed going out.
verses.28:20: The Lord will send upon you famine and hunger, and rebuke in all your works that you will do, until He crushes you and destroys you swiftly, because of your most wicked devices in which you have abandoned Me.
verses.28:21: May the Lord attach pestilence to you, until He consumes you from the land that you will enter to possess.
verses.28:22: May the Lord strike you with destitution, fever and cold, burning and heat, and corrupted air and mildew, and may He pursue you until you perish.
verses.28:23: May the sky that is above you be bronze, and the earth that you tread upon be iron.
verses.28:24: May the Lord give dust as the rain of your land, and from the sky may ash descend upon you, until you are crushed.
verses.28:25: May the Lord hand you over to fall before your enemies; by one way may you go out against them, and by seven flee, and be scattered through all the kingdoms of the earth,
verses.28:26: and may your corpse be food for all the birds of the sky and beasts of the earth, and may there be no one to drive them away.
verses.28:27: May the Lord strike you with the ulcer of Egypt, and strike the part of the body through which excrement is discharged, with scab and itching as well, so that you cannot be cured.
verses.28:28: May the Lord strike you with madness and blindness and frenzy of mind,
verses.28:29: and may you grope at midday just as a blind man is accustomed to grope in darkness, and not direct your ways. And at all times may you endure false accusation and be oppressed by violence, and have no one to rescue you.
verses.28:30: May you take a wife, and another man sleep with her. May you build a house, and not live in it. May you plant a vineyard, and not harvest its grapes.
verses.28:31: May your ox be slaughtered before you, and you not eat from it. May your donkey be seized in your sight, and not be returned to you. May your sheep be given to your enemies, and may there be no one to help you.
verses.28:32: May your sons and your daughters be handed over to another people, while your eyes look on and fail at the sight of them all day long, and may there be no strength in your hand.
verses.28:33: May a people whom you do not know eat the fruits of your land and all your labors, and may you always be enduring false accusation and oppressed every day,
verses.28:34: and stunned at the terror of the things that your eyes will see.
verses.28:35: May the Lord strike you with a most severe ulcer on the knees and on the calves, and may you not be able to be healed from the sole of the foot all the way to the crown of your head.
verses.28:36: The Lord will lead you, and your king whom you set over yourself, into a nation that you and your fathers do not know; and there you will serve foreign gods, wood and stone.
verses.28:37: And you will be ruined, a proverb and a tale to all the peoples to whom the Lord will bring you.
verses.28:38: You will cast much seed into the ground, and you will gather little, because the locusts will devour everything.
verses.28:39: You will plant a vineyard and dig it, and you will not drink wine nor gather anything from it, because it will be laid waste by worms.
verses.28:40: You will have olive trees in all your borders, and you will not anoint yourself with oil, because they will drop off and perish.
verses.28:41: You will father sons and daughters, and you will not enjoy them, because they will be led into captivity.
verses.28:42: Mildew will consume all your trees and the crops of your land.
verses.28:43: The stranger who dwells with you in the land will rise above you and be higher, while you will go down and be lower.
verses.28:44: He will lend to you, and you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.
verses.28:45: And all these curses will come upon you, and pursuing you they will take hold of you until you perish, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God, nor keep His commandments and ceremonies which He commanded you.
verses.28:46: And they will be signs and wonders upon you, and upon your seed forever,
verses.28:47: because you did not serve the Lord your God in joy and gladness of heart, on account of the abundance of all things.
verses.28:48: You will serve your enemy, whom the Lord will send against you, in hunger and thirst and nakedness and all scarcity; and he will place an iron yoke upon your neck until he crushes you.
verses.28:49: The Lord will bring upon you a nation from afar, and from the farthest ends of the earth, in the likeness of an eagle flying with a rush, whose language you cannot understand,
verses.28:50: a most brazen nation, which will show no deference to an old man nor have mercy on a little child,
verses.28:51: and will devour the fruit of your livestock and the crops of your land until you perish, and will not leave you wheat, wine, and oil, herds of oxen and flocks of sheep, until it destroys you,
verses.28:52: and crushes you in all your cities, and your strong and lofty walls, in which you had trust in all your land, are torn down. You will be besieged within your gates in all your land, which the Lord your God will give you,
verses.28:53: and you will eat the fruit of your womb and the flesh of your sons and your daughters, whom the Lord your God has given you, in the distress and devastation with which your enemy will oppress you.
verses.28:54: The delicate and very self-indulgent man among you will begrudge his brother and the wife who lies in his bosom,
verses.28:55: so as not to give them any of the flesh of his sons that he will eat, because he has nothing else in the siege and scarcity with which your enemies will devastate you within all your gates.
verses.28:56: The tender and delicate woman, who was not able to walk upon the earth nor set the sole of her foot because of her excessive softness and tenderness, will begrudge her husband, who lies in her bosom, the flesh of her son and daughter,
verses.28:57: and the discharge of the afterbirth that comes out from between her thighs, and the children who were born in that very hour. For they will eat them secretly because of the scarcity of all things in the siege and devastation with which your enemy will oppress you within your gates.
verses.28:58: If you do not keep and do all the words of this law which are written in this scroll, and fear His glorious and fearsome name, that is, the Lord your God,
verses.28:59: the Lord will increase your plagues and the plagues of your seed, great and persistent plagues, most severe and perpetual sicknesses,
verses.28:60: and He will turn upon you all the afflictions of Egypt, which you feared, and they will cling to you.
verses.28:61: Furthermore, the Lord will bring upon you all ailments and plagues that are not written in the scroll of this law, until He crushes you,
verses.28:62: and you will remain few in number, who previously were like the stars of the sky for multitude, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God.
verses.28:63: And just as the Lord previously rejoiced over you, doing good to you and multiplying you, so He will rejoice in destroying you and overthrowing you, so that you will be taken away from the land that you will enter to possess.
verses.28:64: The Lord will scatter you among all peoples, from the extremity of the earth all the way to its borders; and there you will serve foreign gods, whom neither you nor your fathers know, wood and stones.
verses.28:65: Among those nations also you will not rest, nor will there be rest for the sole of your foot. For there the Lord will give you a fearful heart, and failing eyes, and a soul consumed with sorrow,
verses.28:66: and your life will be as though hanging before you. You will be afraid night and day, and you will not trust in your life.
verses.28:67: In the morning you will say, "Who would give me evening?" and in the evening, "Who would give me morning?" because of the dread of your heart with which you will be terrified, and because of the things that you will see with your eyes.
verses.28:68: The Lord will bring you back in ships to Egypt by the way of which He told you that you should see it no more. There you will be sold to your enemies as male and female slaves, and there will be no one to buy.
verses.28:69: These are the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses to make with the sons of Israel in the land of Moab, besides that covenant which He made with them at Horeb.
verses.29:1: And Moses called all Israel and said to them, "You have seen everything that the Lord did before you in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to his entire land,
verses.29:2: the great trials which your eyes saw, those signs and mighty wonders.
verses.29:3: Yet the Lord has not given you an understanding heart, and eyes that see, and ears that can hear, up to the present day.
verses.29:4: He led you for forty years through the wilderness; your garments did not wear out, nor were the sandals of your feet consumed by age.
verses.29:5: You did not eat bread; you did not drink wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am the Lord your God.
verses.29:6: And you came to this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out, meeting us for battle. And we struck them down,
verses.29:7: and we took their land, and handed it over to Reuben and Gad and to the half-tribe of Manasseh to possess.
verses.29:8: Keep, therefore, the words of this covenant, and fulfill them, so that you may understand everything that you do.
verses.29:9: All of you stand today before the Lord your God: your leaders and tribes, and elders, and teachers, all the people of Israel,
verses.29:10: your children and wives, and the stranger who stays with you in the camp, except the cutters of wood and those who carry water,
verses.29:11: so that you may pass into the covenant of the Lord your God, and into the oath which the Lord your God makes with you today,
verses.29:12: so that He may raise you up for Himself as a people, and He Himself may be your God, just as He spoke to you, and just as He swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.29:13: And not with you alone do I make this covenant and confirm these oaths,
verses.29:14: but with all who are present and absent.
verses.29:15: For you know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we passed through the midst of the nations, passing through which
verses.29:16: you saw the abominations and filth, that is, their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which they worshiped.
verses.29:17: Let there not by chance be among you a man or woman, family or tribe, whose heart is turned away today from the Lord our God, to go and serve the gods of those nations, nor let there be among you a root sprouting gall and bitterness.
verses.29:18: And when he hears the words of this oath, he may bless himself in his heart, saying, 'Peace will be mine, and I will walk in the depravity of my heart,' and the drunken one may consume the thirsty one;
verses.29:19: yet the Lord will not forgive him, but then above all His fury and jealousy will smoke against that man, and all the curses that are written in this scroll will settle upon him, and the Lord will blot out his name under heaven,
verses.29:20: and consume him to destruction out of all the tribes of Israel, according to the curses that are contained in the book of this law and covenant.
verses.29:21: And the following generation will say, and the children who will be born afterward, and the foreigners who come from far away, seeing the plagues of that land and the sicknesses with which the Lord has afflicted it,
verses.29:22: burning it with sulfur and the heat of salt, so that it is no longer sown, nor does anything green sprout, as an example of the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the Lord overthrew in His anger and fury.
verses.29:23: And all the nations will say, 'Why has the Lord done so to this land? What is this immense anger of His fury?'
verses.29:24: And they will answer, 'Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord, which He made with their fathers, when He brought them out of the land of Egypt,
verses.29:25: and they served foreign gods, and worshiped those whom they did not know, and to whom they had not been assigned;
verses.29:26: therefore the fury of the Lord grew angry against this land, so as to bring upon it all the curses that are written in this scroll;
verses.29:27: and He drove them out of their land in anger and in fury, and in the greatest indignation, and cast them into a foreign land, as is proven today.'
verses.29:28: The hidden things belong to the Lord our God; the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, so that we may do all the words of this law."
verses.30:1: "Therefore, when all these words have come upon you, the blessing or the curse which I have set in your sight, and you are led by repentance of your heart among all the nations into which the Lord your God has scattered you,
verses.30:2: and you return to Him and obey His commands, just as I command you today, with your children, with all your heart and with all your soul,
verses.30:3: the Lord your God will bring back your captivity, and will have mercy on you, and will gather you again from all the peoples among whom He previously scattered you.
verses.30:4: If you have been dispersed to the poles of heaven, from there the Lord your God will draw you back,
verses.30:5: and will take you, and will bring you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you will obtain it; and blessing you, He will make you greater in number than your fathers were.
verses.30:6: The Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, so that you may love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may be able to live.
verses.30:7: And He will turn all these curses upon your enemies, and upon those who hate and persecute you.
verses.30:8: But you will return and listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and do all the commandments that I command you today;
verses.30:9: and the Lord your God will make you abound in all the works of your hands, in the offspring of your womb, and in the fruit of your livestock, in the fertility of your land, and in the bounty of all things. For the Lord will return to rejoice over you in all good things, just as He rejoiced in your fathers,
verses.30:10: if indeed you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and keep His precepts and ceremonies, which are written in this law, and return to the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
verses.30:11: This commandment, which I command you today, is not above you, nor placed far away,
verses.30:12: nor situated in heaven, so that you might say, 'Who among us is able to ascend to heaven, so that he may bring it down to us, and we may hear it and fulfill it in deed?'
verses.30:13: nor placed across the sea, so that you might make excuses and say, 'Who from among us will be able to cross the sea, and bring it all the way to us, so that we may be able to hear and do what has been commanded?'
verses.30:14: but the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, so that you may do it.
verses.30:15: Consider that today I have set in your sight life and good, and on the contrary, death and evil,
verses.30:16: so that you may love the Lord your God, and walk in His ways, and keep His commandments, ceremonies, and judgments, and you may live, and He may multiply you and bless you in the land that you will enter to possess.
verses.30:17: But if your heart turns away, and you refuse to listen, and, deceived by error, you worship foreign gods and serve them,
verses.30:18: I declare to you today that you will perish, and will remain for a short time in the land which, once the Jordan has been crossed, you will enter to possess.
verses.30:19: I call heaven and earth as witnesses today that I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. Choose life, therefore, so that both you and your seed may live,
verses.30:20: and you may love the Lord your God, and obey His voice, and hold fast to Him (for He Himself is your life and the length of your days), so that you may dwell in the land concerning which the Lord swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, that He would give it to them."
verses.31:1: Therefore Moses went and spoke all these words to the whole of Israel,
verses.31:2: and he said to them, "I am one hundred twenty years old today; I am no longer able to go out and come in, especially since the Lord has also said to me, 'You will not cross this Jordan.'
verses.31:3: Therefore the Lord your God will cross over ahead of you; He Himself will destroy all these nations in your sight, and you will possess them; and this Joshua will cross over ahead of you, just as the Lord has spoken.
verses.31:4: And the Lord will do to them just as He did to Sihon and Og, kings of the Amorites, and to their land, and He will destroy them.
verses.31:5: Therefore, when He has handed these over to you as well, you will do to them in the same way, just as I have commanded you.
verses.31:6: Act courageously and be strengthened; do not be afraid, nor be terrified at the sight of them, for the Lord your God Himself is your leader, and He will neither leave nor abandon you."
verses.31:7: And Moses called Joshua and said to him in the presence of all Israel, "Be strengthened and be resolute, for you will bring this people into the land that the Lord swore He would give to their fathers, and you will divide it by lot.
verses.31:8: And the Lord, who is your leader, will Himself be with you; He will neither leave nor abandon you; do not be afraid, nor be terrified."
verses.31:9: So Moses wrote this law and handed it over to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and to all the elders of Israel.
verses.31:10: And he commanded them, saying, "After seven years, in the year of remission, at the solemn feast of Tabernacles,
verses.31:11: when all those from Israel assemble to appear in the sight of the Lord your God in the place that the Lord will choose, you will read the words of this law in the presence of all Israel, in their hearing,
verses.31:12: and with all the people gathered together as one, both men and women, little ones, and foreigners who are within your gates, so that as they listen they may learn and fear the Lord your God, and keep and fulfill all the words of this law;
verses.31:13: so that their children also, who now do not know, may be able to hear and may fear the Lord their God all the days in which they live in the land that you are going to obtain after crossing the Jordan."
verses.31:14: And the Lord said to Moses, "Look, the days of your death are near; call Joshua, and stand in the tabernacle of the testimony, so that I may command him." So Moses and Joshua went and stood in the tabernacle of the testimony.
verses.31:15: And the Lord appeared there in a pillar of cloud, which stood at the entrance of the tabernacle.
verses.31:16: And the Lord said to Moses, "Look, you will sleep with your fathers, and this people will rise up and prostitute themselves after foreign gods in the land into which they are entering so that they may dwell in it; there they will abandon Me and nullify the covenant that I made with them.
verses.31:17: And My fury will rage against them on that day, and I will abandon them and hide My face from them, and they will be for devouring; all evils and afflictions will find them, so that they will say on that day, 'Truly, because God is not with me, these evils have found me.'
verses.31:18: But I will hide and conceal My face on that day on account of all the evils that they have done, because they have followed foreign gods.
verses.31:19: Now therefore, write this song for yourselves and teach it to the sons of Israel, so that they may keep it in memory and sing it with their mouths, and this song may be a witness for Me among the sons of Israel.
verses.31:20: For I will bring them into the land for which I swore to their fathers, flowing with milk and honey. And when they have eaten and been satisfied and grown fat, they will turn aside to foreign gods and serve them, and they will revile Me and nullify My covenant.
verses.31:21: After many evils and afflictions have found them, this song, which no forgetfulness will erase from the mouth of their seed, will answer them as a witness. For I know their thoughts, what they are about to do today, before I bring them into the land that I have promised them."
verses.31:22: Therefore Moses wrote the song and taught it to the sons of Israel.
verses.31:23: And the Lord commanded Joshua son of Nun and said, "Be strengthened and be resolute, for you will bring the sons of Israel into the land that I have promised, and I will be with you."
verses.31:24: Therefore, after Moses had written the words of this law in a scroll and completed them,
verses.31:25: he commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, saying,
verses.31:26: "Take this book and place it at the side of the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, so that it may be there as a witness against you.
verses.31:27: For I know your contentiousness and your most stubborn neck. While I am still alive and walking with you, you have always acted contentiously against the Lord; how much more when I am dead?
verses.31:28: Assemble to me all the elders throughout your tribes, and the teachers, and I will speak these words in their hearing, and I will call upon heaven and earth against them.
verses.31:29: For I know that after my death you will act wickedly and quickly turn aside from the way that I have commanded you; and evils will meet you in the final time, when you do evil in the sight of the Lord, so as to provoke Him through the works of your hands."
verses.31:30: Therefore Moses spoke, in the hearing of the entire assembly of Israel, the words of this song, and completed them to the very end.
verses.32:1: Hear, heavens, what I speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
verses.32:2: May my teaching condense like rain, may my speech flow like dew, like a shower upon vegetation, and like drops upon the grass.
verses.32:3: For I will call upon the name of the Lord; give magnificence to our God.
verses.32:4: The works of God are perfect, and all His ways are judgments; God is faithful and without any iniquity, just and upright.
verses.32:5: They have sinned against Him, and are not His children in filth: a crooked and perverse generation.
verses.32:6: Do you repay these things to the Lord, you foolish and unwise people? Is He not Himself your Father, who possessed you, and made and created you?
verses.32:7: Remember the ancient days, consider each generation; ask your father, and he will declare it to you; your elders, and they will tell you.
verses.32:8: When the Most High was dividing the nations, when He was separating the sons of Adam, He established the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.
verses.32:9: But the portion of the Lord is His people; Jacob is the cord of His inheritance.
verses.32:10: He found him in a desert land, in a place of horror and vast desolation; He led him around and taught him, and guarded him like the pupil of His eye.
verses.32:11: Like an eagle urging its young to fly and hovering over them, He spread out His wings and took him up, and carried him on His shoulders.
verses.32:12: The Lord alone was his guide, and there was no foreign god with him.
verses.32:13: He set him upon a high land, so that he might eat the fruits of the fields, so that he might suck honey from the rock and oil from the hardest stone;
verses.32:14: butter from the herd and milk from the sheep, with the fat of lambs and of rams, the sons of Bashan, and male goats with the marrow of wheat, and might drink the purest blood of the grape.
verses.32:15: The beloved grew fat and kicked; grown fat, grown plump, grown broad, he abandoned God his Maker, and departed from God his Savior.
verses.32:16: They provoked Him with foreign gods, and with abominations they stirred Him up to anger.
verses.32:17: They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods whom they did not know; new and recent ones came, whom their fathers did not worship.
verses.32:18: You have abandoned the God who fathered you, and have forgotten the Lord your Creator.
verses.32:19: The Lord saw, and was stirred up to anger, because His sons and daughters provoked Him.
verses.32:20: And He said, "I will hide My face from them, and consider their final end; for it is a perverse generation, and unfaithful children.
verses.32:21: They themselves provoked Me with what was not God, and angered Me with their vanities; and I will provoke them with what is not a people, and with a foolish nation I will anger them.
verses.32:22: A fire has been kindled in My fury, and it will burn all the way to the lowest depths of the underworld; and it will devour the earth with its growth, and burn up the foundations of the mountains.
verses.32:23: I will gather evils upon them, and I will use up My arrows on them.
verses.32:24: They will be consumed by famine, and birds will devour them with a most bitter bite; I will send the teeth of beasts against them, with the fury of things crawling upon the earth, and of serpents.
verses.32:25: Outside, the sword will lay them waste, and inside, terror: the young man together with the virgin, the nursing child with the aged man.
verses.32:26: I said, 'Where are they? I will make the remembrance of them cease from among mankind.'
verses.32:27: But because of the wrath of the enemies I delayed, so that their foes might not perhaps become arrogant and say, 'Our exalted hand, and not the Lord, has done all these things.'"
verses.32:28: It is a nation without counsel, and without prudence.
verses.32:29: If only they were wise, and understood, and foresaw the final end!
verses.32:30: How could one pursue a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight? Is it not for this reason, because their God sold them, and the Lord shut them up?
verses.32:31: For our God is not like their gods, and our enemies are judges.
verses.32:32: From the vineyard of Sodom is their vineyard, and from the outskirts of Gomorrah; their grape is a grape of gall, and their clusters are most bitter.
verses.32:33: Their wine is the gall of dragons, and the incurable venom of asps.
verses.32:34: "Are not these things stored up with Me, and sealed in My treasuries?
verses.32:35: Vengeance is Mine, and I will repay in time, so that their foot may slip; the day of destruction is near, and the times are hurrying to arrive."
verses.32:36: The Lord will judge His people, and will have compassion on His servants; He will see that the hand has been weakened, and those shut up have also failed, and those remaining have been consumed.
verses.32:37: And He will say, "Where are their gods, in whom they had confidence,
verses.32:38: from whose sacrifices they ate the fat and drank the wine of drink offerings? Let them rise up and aid you, and protect you in distress.
verses.32:39: See that I alone am, and there is no other god besides Me: I will kill, and I will make alive; I will strike, and I will heal, and there is no one who can rescue from My hand.
verses.32:40: I will lift up My hand to heaven and say, 'I live forever.'
verses.32:41: If I sharpen My sword like lightning, and My hand takes hold of judgment, I will render vengeance to My foes, and I will repay those who hate Me.
verses.32:42: I will make My arrows drunk with blood, and My sword will devour flesh, from the gore of the killed and from the captivity, of the bared head of the enemies."
verses.32:43: Praise His people, nations, because He will avenge the blood of His servants, and He will repay vengeance upon their foes, and He will be merciful to the land of His people.
verses.32:44: So Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the ears of the people, he himself and Joshua the son of Nun.
verses.32:45: And he completed all these sayings, speaking to all Israel,
verses.32:46: and he said to them, "Set your hearts on all the words that I testify to you today, so that you may command your children to keep and do them, and to fulfill all things of this law that are written;
verses.32:47: for they have not been commanded to you in vain, but so that each one might live in them; and doing these things, you may continue for a long time in the land that, once the Jordan has been crossed, you are entering to possess."
verses.32:48: And the Lord spoke to Moses on that same day, saying,
verses.32:49: "Go up onto this mountain Abarim, that is, the Crossing, onto Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab opposite Jericho, and see the land of Canaan, which I will hand over to the sons of Israel to obtain, and die on the mountain.
verses.32:50: Ascending it, you will be joined to your people, just as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was united with his people;
verses.32:51: because you transgressed against Me in the midst of the sons of Israel at the waters of Contradiction in Kadesh of the wilderness of Zin, and you did not sanctify Me among the sons of Israel.
verses.32:52: From across, you will see the land that I will give to the sons of Israel, and you will not enter into it."
verses.33:1: This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the sons of Israel before his death.
verses.33:2: And he said: "The Lord came from Sinai, and from Seir He rose upon us; He appeared from Mount Paran, and with Him were thousands of holy ones. In His right hand was a fiery law.
verses.33:3: He loved the peoples; all the holy ones are in His hand, and those who draw near to His feet will receive from His teaching.
verses.33:4: Moses commanded a law for us, an inheritance of the multitude of Jacob.
verses.33:5: There will be a king with the most upright one, when the leaders of the people are gathered together with the tribes of Israel.
verses.33:6: Let Reuben live and not die, and let him be small in number."
verses.33:7: This is the blessing of Judah: "Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him in to his people; his hands will fight for him, and his helper will be against his adversaries."
verses.33:8: Of Levi he also said: "Your perfection and Your teaching belong to Your holy man, whom You proved in testing and judged at the waters of Contradiction.
verses.33:9: He said to his father and to his mother, 'I do not know you,' and to his brothers, 'I do not recognize you,' and they did not know their sons. These kept Your word and observed Your covenant,
verses.33:10: Your judgments, Jacob, and Your law, Israel. They will place incense in Your wrath and a burnt offering upon Your altar.
verses.33:11: Bless, Lord, his strength, and accept the works of his hands. Strike the backs of his enemies, and let those who hate him not rise up."
verses.33:12: And of Benjamin he said: "The most beloved of the Lord will dwell confidently in Him; as in a bridal chamber he will remain all day long, and between His shoulders he will rest."
verses.33:13: Of Joseph he also said: "From the blessing of the Lord is his land, from the fruits of heaven and the dew, and from the deep lying beneath,
verses.33:14: from the fruits of the yields of the sun and moon,
verses.33:15: from the summit of the ancient mountains, from the fruits of the eternal hills,
verses.33:16: and from the crops of the earth and from its fullness. May the blessing of Him who appeared in the bush come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazirite among his brothers.
verses.33:17: His beauty is like that of a firstborn bull; his horns are the horns of a rhinoceros. With them he will scatter the nations to the ends of the earth. These are the multitudes of Ephraim, and these are the thousands of Manasseh."
verses.33:18: And of Zebulun he said: "Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.
verses.33:19: They will call peoples to the mountain; there they will offer sacrifices of righteousness. They will suck the overflowing of the sea like milk, and the hidden treasures of the sands."
verses.33:20: And of Gad he said: "Blessed is Gad in breadth; like a lion he rested, and he seized the arm and the crown of the head.
verses.33:21: And he saw his preeminence, that in his portion the teacher was laid up, who was with the leaders of the people, and carried out the righteous deeds of the Lord and his judgment with Israel."
verses.33:22: Of Dan he also said: "Dan is a lion's cub; he will flow abundantly from Bashan."
verses.33:23: And of Naphtali he said: "Naphtali will fully enjoy abundance and will be full of the blessings of the Lord; he will possess the sea and the south."
verses.33:24: Of Asher he also said: "Blessed is Asher among sons; let him be pleasing to his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil.
verses.33:25: Iron and bronze are his footwear. As the days of your youth, so also will your old age be.
verses.33:26: There is no other god like the God of the most upright one, the rider of heaven, your helper. By His majesty the clouds run to and fro,
verses.33:27: His dwelling place is above, and underneath are the everlasting arms; He will cast out the enemy from before your face, and He will say, 'Be crushed!'
verses.33:28: Israel will dwell confidently, and alone. The eye of Jacob is in a land of grain and wine, and the heavens will grow dark with dew.
verses.33:29: Blessed are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people who are saved in the Lord? He is the shield of your help and the sword of your glory; your enemies will deny you, and you will tread upon their necks."
verses.34:1: So Moses went up from the plains of Moab onto Mount Nebo, to the summit of Pisgah opposite Jericho; and the Lord showed him all the land of Gilead as far as Dan,
verses.34:2: and all Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah as far as the farthest sea,
verses.34:3: and the southern part, and the breadth of the plain of Jericho, the city of palms, as far as Zoar.
verses.34:4: And the Lord said to him: "This is the land about which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, 'To your seed I will give it.' You have seen it with your eyes, and you will not cross over to it."
verses.34:5: And Moses, the servant of the Lord, died there in the land of Moab, at the command of the Lord;
verses.34:6: and He buried him in the valley of the land of Moab opposite Peor; and no man has known his tomb to the present day.
verses.34:7: Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eye did not grow dim, nor were his teeth loosened.
verses.34:8: And the sons of Israel wept for him in the plains of Moab for thirty days; and the days of lamentation of those mourning Moses were completed.
verses.34:9: Now Joshua the son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands upon him. And the sons of Israel obeyed him and did just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.34:10: And no prophet has arisen again in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,
verses.34:11: in all the signs and wonders which He sent through him to perform in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to his entire land,
verses.34:12: and all the mighty hand and the great marvels that Moses performed before all Israel.

notes.1:1: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew place name Suph as "the Red Sea" (mare Rubrum) and translates the place name Di-zahab literally as a descriptive clause, "where gold is very plentiful" (ubi auri est plurimum).
notes.1:15: The Vulgate adapts the Israelite ranks into Roman military titles (tribunos, centuriones, quinquagenarios, decanos) and closes with "who would teach you each individual matter" (qui docerent vos singula), where the Hebrew reads "and officers for your tribes."
notes.1:24: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew place name Nahal Eshcol literally as "the Valley of the Cluster" (Vallem botri).
notes.1:25: The explanatory clause "so that they might show its fertility" (ut ostenderent ubertatem) is a Vulgate-distinct addition not present in the Hebrew text.
notes.1:37: The opening clause "Nor is the indignation against the people surprising" (Nec miranda indignatio in populum) is a distinctive Vulgate expansion not found in the Hebrew text.
notes.2:11: The Vulgate renders Hebrew Rephaim throughout chapters 2-3 (2:11, 2:20; 3:11, 3:13) as gigantes ("giants"), and here explicitly links the Emim's stature to the Anakim with the result clause "so tall that, as of the lineage of the Anakim, they were thought to be like giants."
notes.2:13: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, where God commands Israel to rise and cross the brook Zered before Moses reports that they crossed it, the Vulgate presents the entire verse as Moses' narrative: "Rising, therefore, to cross the stream of Zered, we came to it."
notes.2:23: Following the Septuagint tradition, the Vulgate preserves three distinctive proper names here: Hevaeos ("Hivites", where the Hebrew has "Avvim"), Haserim treated as a place name ("Hazerim", Hebrew "villages"), and Cappadoces / Cappadocia ("Cappadocians" / "Cappadocia", where the Hebrew has "Caphtorim" / "Caphtor").
notes.2:25: The Vulgate expands the Hebrew verb for writhing in anguish into an explicit simile, in morem parturientium ("like women in labor").
notes.3:11: Where the Hebrew asks rhetorically whether Og's bed is not in Rabbah and specifies "by the cubit of a man," the Vulgate states Monstratur lectus ejus ferreus ("His iron bed is shown") and clarifies the measure as ad mensuram cubiti virilis manus ("according to the measure of the cubit of a man's hand").
notes.3:14: The explanatory gloss id est, Villas Jair ("that is, the Villages of Jair") is a Vulgate addition translating the Hebrew name Havvoth-jair for Latin readers.
notes.3:17: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew "Salt Sea" with a superlative clause, quod est salsissimum ("which is the saltiest"), and reads terminos Cenereth ("the borders of Chinnereth") rather than "the border, from Chinnereth."
notes.3:29: Rather than transliterating the Hebrew place name Beth-peor, the Vulgate translates Beth ("house") as fanum ("shrine"), rendering the site as fanum Phogor ("the shrine of Peor").
notes.4:5: The Vulgate reads Scitis ("You know"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "See/Look."
notes.4:19: The Vulgate reads quæ creavit ... in ministerium ("what the Lord your God created for the service"), whereas the Hebrew reads "which the Lord your God allotted" to all the peoples.
notes.4:29: The Vulgate reads tota tribulatione animæ tuæ ("with all the affliction of your soul") where the Hebrew has simply "with all your soul."
notes.4:46: The Vulgate renders Beth-peor as fanum Phogor ("the shrine of Peor") and ends the sentence after Moyses., making "The sons of Israel also, having come out of Egypt" the subject of "took possession" in verse 47 rather than pairing them with Moses in striking down Sihon.
notes.4:48: Mount Sion (Latin montem Sion, Hebrew Si'on) is an alternative name for Mount Hermon in the north and is distinct from Mount Zion in Jerusalem.
notes.5:1: Latin 'caeremonias' ("ceremonies," used consistently throughout chs. 5-6) is the Vulgate's characteristic rendering of the Hebrew term chuqqim ("statutes").
notes.5:4: The Vulgate reads 'nobis' ("to us"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "to you" (plural).
notes.5:5: Latin 'sequester et medius' ("mediator and intermediary") expands the Hebrew "standing [between]" into a double mediatorial expression.
notes.5:14: The Vulgate inserts the explanatory gloss 'id est, requies' ("that is, the rest") to explain the loanword 'sabbati' for Latin readers.
notes.5:17: In this Latin source text, 'neque moechaberis' ("And you shall not commit adultery") stands at v. 17 and 'Non occides' ("You shall not kill") at v. 18, reversing the order of the Hebrew text and standard Vulgate editions (note the connective 'neque' in v. 17 and capitalized 'Non' in v. 18).
notes.6:4: Latin 'Dominus Deus noster, Dominus unus est' uses a single verb 'est' and can be read either as "the Lord our God is one Lord" (taking 'Dominus unus' as predicate) or "the Lord our God, the Lord is one."
notes.6:8: Latin 'eruntque et movebuntur' ("and they shall be and move") stands where the Hebrew has a rare noun for bands or frontlets; likewise, v. 9 reads 'in limine, et ostiis' ("on the threshold and the doors") rather than Hebrew "doorposts" and "gates."
notes.6:11: In this Latin text, the material corresponding to standard verses 11-13 is combined under v. 11; note also the Vulgate-distinct readings 'quas non exstruxisti' ("which you did not construct," vs. Hebrew "fill") and 'illi soli' ("Him alone," matching the Septuagint and Matt 4:10).
notes.6:16: Latin 'in loco tentationis' ("at the place of testing") translates the Hebrew place name Massah according to its meaning.
notes.6:25: Latin 'Eritque nostri misericors' ("And He will be merciful to us") aligns with the Septuagint in reading "mercy" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "righteousness" ("it will be righteousness for us").
notes.7:5: The Vulgate renders the Canaanite cult objects as statuas ("statues") and lucos ("groves"), whereas the Hebrew text refers to sacred pillars and Asherah poles.
notes.7:10: The Vulgate expands the Hebrew idiom "to his face" into the explicit temporal rendering statim ... protinus eis restituens quod merentur ("immediately ... at once paying them back what they deserve").
notes.7:23: The Vulgate reads et interficiet illos ("and He will put them to death"), whereas the Hebrew text reads "and throw them into great confusion."
notes.7:25: This Latin text reads Domini tui ("your Lord") without Dei ("God"), and reads de quibus facta sunt ("from which they are made") rather than the Hebrew "which is on them."
